383YE Spring Equinox Synod judgements.d: No change of doctrine, veto or recognition was sought. The General Assembly agreed not to uphold new recognitions or doctrinal changes for up to a year while talks with Sumaah continue. Many assemblies criticised or defended the Grey Pilgrims. Enacted mandates sent citizens to repurpose the idols of Almodin Oktístis, resettled Zenith's refugees, rewarded those guiding freed Dubhtraig orcs to Skarsind, and opened Marcher billets to Imperial armies. Medea Ruth was condemned for heresy. Several inquisitions were called, including one into the Senator for Temeschwar. Viviane de Coeurdefer and Ser Ancél Watcher became Cardinals of Ambition and Vigilance. The virtue fund closed at 36 Thrones, 6 Crowns and 15 Rings.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish assembly sent Ser Ancél Watcher with troubadours and questing knights to track down Druj miasma pillars in Ossium, and condemned the use of cruel armies. It also honoured the houses that raised the Gates of Adamant and called House Minos nobles to inquisition over aiding Asaveans against rebelling slaves.
n.Druj: An enacted Dawnish mandate set questing knights hunting the Druj miasma pillars in Ossium. Mandates from Highguard and Urizen found homes for Urizeni refugees displaced by the Druj.
n.Grendel: After the Imperial raid on Dubhtraig, the Synod moved to help the slaves freed there reach the Empire. It also thanked the Asaveans at Feroz for protecting Freeborn citizens from the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Highborn priests stood at the centre of the Grey Pilgrims controversy, and Sister Lilith of the Chantry was called to inquisition. The Highborn assembly enacted a mandate offering Urizeni refugees sanctuary in Reikos and urged its commanders to liberate Tamarbode from the Eternal Llofir.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs enacted a mandate rewarding those who bring freed Dubhtraig orcs home to Skarsind, at a cost to the nation's production. Their assembly also urged engagement with the Sand Fishers and praised the Coven of Crows.
n.Jotun: Wintermark's assembly declared that becoming a Jotun thrall is not heroic, urged that thralls be spared so they could come home, and lamented the Jotun occupation of Sermersuaq. The Marches urged Mournwold orcs who were formerly Jotun thralls to become Marcher citizens.
n.Navarr: The Navarr assembly rejected the Grey Pilgrims' critique of national faith and called for a new army to strike at the vallorn. The General Assembly urged action in Liathaven and Brocéliande and recognised Seren in Miaren as a city of worth.
n.The League: The League assembly narrowly called for Imperial Bourse seats in League territory to become national seats again, and invited study of the Giselle frogs of Sarvos. A mandate consecrated the Colossus of Sarvos to Pride, and the Senator for Temeschwar was called to inquisition over the Oktístis idols.
n.The Marches: An enacted Marcher mandate lets any Imperial army billet in Marcher territory with access to the Imperial Breadbasket. The assembly also invited Mournwold orcs to become Marchers, urged folk to shun the Grey Pilgrims and vindicated Will Talbot, General of the Drakes.
n.Urizen: Refugees from Zenith are to settle in Redoubt and Morrow under an enacted Urizeni mandate, while Highguard offered others sanctuary in Reikos. The Synod also funded a School of War honouring Morrow's defenders and vindicated Tolamy for saving the injured at Atheneum Spire.
n.Varushka: Varushka enacted a mandate urging its people towards the riches of mines and forests, and welcomed the Ketsov and others in Ossium as Varushkans. It named Father Drakov Tender of the Hearth and recognised Zoria's original shrine in the Vale of Gniejezdo.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's assembly cautioned against narrowing Heroism to Steinr 'honour' and called Krampus subservience idolatry. It also encouraged pilgrimage to Isenbrad's tomb in Runegrott and appointed Ursa Hendel Hearth Crow Keeper of the Rest.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind is the intended new home of the slaves freed from Dubhtraig, and an enacted mandate rewards those who guide them there. Preachers from Skarsind were urged to travel with the Great Forest orcs to aid the liberated.

383YE Spring Equinox winds of fortune.d: Navarr defenders, aided by Dawn, Highguard, forest orcs and Tharim, struggled to hold Elerael and Boar's Dell against the vallorn. Ossium joined Varushka but faced unresolved threats. Urizen thanked its allies and weighed what to do with those rescued from Zenith. The Druj threatened to slaughter yeofolk children in Dawnguard if the Empire kept invading the Mallum. Refugees from Dubhtraig were stranded across the Empire. Grendel pirates of Attar raided shipping. Wardens smashed Janon's statue in Temeschwar. Further entries covered the Liberty Pact sanctions, Sarcophan trade proposals, a Wintermark rune forge proposal and orc diplomacy. Sixteen Synod mandates were upheld, and Frederick di Sarvos faced inquisition.

n.Dawn: Dawn faced a Druj threat to slaughter the yeofolk children held in Dawnguard, with a possible rescue foray into the Barrens. Its national assembly also sent Ranae de Rondell with liao to rally knights and witches to Brocéliande, and Weirwater suffered a subtle curse.
n.Druj: The Druj issued an ultimatum to kill the Dawnish prisoners in Dawnguard if the Empire continued invading the Mallum. They still held Zenith and were pressing into Spiral.
n.Grendel: The Grendel armada was focused on invading Feroz while Attar pirates raided Imperial shipping. Enraged by Imperial raids, the Salt Lords reportedly offered bounties on Imperial vessels, perhaps overreaching enough to give the Empire an opening in the Bay.
n.Highguard: Highguard was thanked by Urizen for its aid and its congregations were urged to help defend Brocéliande. Several Highborn mandates shaped the grey pilgrimage, while its citizens were urged to withhold white granite from the Bourse auction until the Cinderpath Exchange is built.
n.Imperial Orcs: Some two thousand slaves freed from Dubhtraig were offered homes in Skarsind among the Imperial Orcs, but were stranded across the Empire after a harsh winter. Skywise Tulva's mandate urged them to settle there and in time become Imperial Orcs.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the Empire's orc neighbours, alongside a reference to former Jotun thralls and some details about Jotun-held Liathaven.
n.Navarr: The Navarr faced an ever-stronger vallorn assault on their liberated lands in Brocéliande, with allies rallying and Tharim and the General of Day offering further help. Grey pilgrims walking the trods also aided the Navarr's great quest.
n.The Brass Coast: Feroz faced a Grendel invasion and Brass Coast merchant shipping was threatened by Attar pirates. The nation was also tied to Sarcophan trade proposals and to the Cinderpath developments.
n.The League: Urizen urged its people to thank League generals. Sarcophan families proposed a trading enclave in Sarvos, wardens destroyed the idolatrous statue of Janon in Temeschwar, and ships from Tassato and Sarvos faced pirate raids.
n.The Marches: Marchers worked out practical ways for farms to billet and feed armies, Marcher or not, if the Synod approved. The Landskeepers also showed their support for keeping Rivers Run Red under interdiction.
n.Thule: Relations with the Thule of Otkodov suffered a sudden frost. Otkodov was also among the slaving nations placed under sanctions by the Liberty Pact.
n.Urizen: Urizen's National Assembly thanked Varushka, Highguard and the League and controversially welcomed would-be Urizen, even orcs. The nation must also decide whether those rescued from Zenith should wait to return or resettle, depending on whether it consolidates Morrow or tries to retake Zenith.
n.Varushka: Varushka absorbed Ossium, becoming the largest Imperial nation, and was presented with prosperity opportunities. Belakov, the Wolf of Karsk, was sent to examine the freed slaves of Ossium, and a Sarcophan enclave was proposed in Karsk.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark had the chance to build a new rune forge to reclaim the runesmiths' lost prestige, and the hylje offered gifts including crystal mana. Severi Jarlmarison's mandate let Winterfolk turn congregations into military units.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Dawn mandate reminded the people of Semmerholm and Astolat of the Navarr's sacrifices against the vallorn.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Jorma Steelhail's mandate urged that Bastion and the Sumaah city of Timoj be seen as equals in the Way.
t.Bay of Catazar: Attar pirates kept raiding Imperial shipping in the Bay and the Salt Lords claimed mastery of it. Their overconfidence may have given the Empire an opportunity to dominate the Bay.
t.Brocéliande: The vallorn threw more and more of its power against the Navarr-liberated lands of Brocéliande. Dawn, Highguard, forest orcs and Tharim aided the defence, and Synod mandates rallied further support.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel armada was noted to be focused on its invasion of Feroz.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: some details about Hercynia were given alongside the Brocéliande news.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's guilds, free companies and Holberg itself were tagged as interested in trade opportunities and the Ossium situation.
t.Karsk: Sarcophan families proposed turning a ruined location in Karsk into a large trading enclave, and the Wolf of Karsk was charged with vetting the freed slaves of Ossium.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: some details about Liathaven were given alongside the Brocéliande news.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: a recent Imperial raid on Mareave was among those that enraged the Salt Lords.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's recent gains in restoring Morrow were one option it might choose to consolidate.
t.Ossium: Newly conquered Ossium became part of Varushka, with settlers arriving and the egregore finding new citizens. The Ketsov, the Sand Fishers, the Crawling Depths and a miasma of terror remained unresolved.
t.Otkodov: Imperial relations with the Thule of Otkodov frosted over and the territory was placed under Liberty Pact sanctions. Otkodov is also where Wintermark's captured runesmiths were taken long ago.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: residents of Reikos were tagged as concerned by the season's Winds of Magic.
t.Sarvos: Sarcophan families proposed turning a ruined location in Sarvos into a large trading enclave, and merchant ships out of Sarvos faced Grendel pirate raids.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Dawn mandate reminded the people of Semmerholm and Astolat of the Navarr's sacrifices against the vallorn.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was offered as a home for slaves freed from Dubhtraig, and Skywise Tulva's mandate urged them to settle there, though many were stranded across the Empire.
t.Spiral: Spiral remained a grim, contested land facing a Druj advance. Urizen had to choose whether to blunt that advance or commit to retaking Zenith.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: merchant vessels from Tassato were listed among those threatened by Attar pirates.
t.Temeschwar: Inspired by the Cardinal of Pride's condemnation of idolatry, a warden fellowship reduced Temeschwar's statue of Janon to rubble.
t.Weirwater: A subtle curse fell on the Dawnish folk of Weirwater, as covered in the Winds of Magic.
t.Zenith: Imperial heroes rescued more than half of the Urizen imprisoned by the Druj in Zenith, which remained under Druj control as Urizen weighed an attempt to retake it.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Navarr defenders and their allies continued to hold Boar's Dell against the vallorn's strengthening assault.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Elerael remained on the front line as the vallorn brought ever more power against its Navarr defenders.

383YE Spring Equinox winds of war.d: Freed slaves left for Skarsind, and the Broken Shore orcs cannot raise an army in Mareave for a year. Morrow was retaken without casualties, and the Citadel Guard stopped declining. Raiders rescued two-thirds of Zenith's captives. Dawn, Varushka and five Thule armies took Nearweald and the Drownbark Forest. Navarr, aided by Dawn, Highguard and Tharim, held the vallorn in Brocéliande. The Quiet Step and Strong Reeds blunted the Lasambrian Jotun in Segura. Imperial armies took the Ford of Berusen and reached four-tenths of Stark, where the Jotun finished the Tusks of the Lion. The Druj took Ossuary, Screed and the Legacy. Four Sentinel Gate conjunctions were identified.

n.Dawn: Dawnish soldiers stormed Beoraidh's garrison towers, and four Dawnish armies completed the conquest of Ossium alongside the Thule without the aid of the Fields of Glory. Questing knights helped hold the vallorn in Brocéliande, and Dawnish warbands freed captured Highborn soldiers in Zenith.
n.Druj: The Druj abandoned Morrow and were driven entirely out of Ossium, losing Orieb. In return they poured some thirty thousand orcs into Spiral, seizing Ossuary, Screed and the Legacy and nearly retaking Apulus, while keeping their grip on Zenith.
n.Grendel: The Grendel lost their half-built Beoraidh fortress and their coliseum, and cannot raise an army in Mareave for a year. Their armada, however, conquered the Cazar Straits and Oranseri, captured Bramar, looted widely and enslaved Freeborn citizens.
n.Highguard: Highborn soldiers took Beoraidh's towers after the raid set out from Necropolis, and congregations sent warriors and supplies to Brocéliande. The Zenith raid returned 250 troops to each of the Granite Pillar, the Valiant Pegasus and the Seventh Wave.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun marched home to Skarsind while three thousand furloughed reavers led the Beoraidh raid. About 2,500 freed orcs will settle in Skarsind and could one day form the core of a third army. The Summer Storm lost many soldiers beneath the ice of the Atkonaroq.
n.Jotun: The Bear Who Swims came nine-tenths of the way to conquering West Ranging. In Segura the Lasambrian Jotun held Anduzjasse but fell back around Anduz. In Sermersuaq the Jotun lost Atalaq, Sealtoq and the Ford of Berusen, but completed the Tusks of the Lion castle in Stark.
n.Navarr: With help from Dawn, Highguard and Tharim, Navarr bands saved the Broch and held back the vallorn in Brocéliande, though Tharim's feasting costs Miaren, Therunin and Hercynia. Bonering striding was driven from Liathaven, while the Quiet Step and Black Thorns fought in Segura and Stark.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn corsairs spearheaded the landing at Beoraidh, but the Grendel conquered the Cazar Straits and Oranseri, looting and enslaving Freeborn and seizing two Bourse offices. Segura was defended by Imperial armies, and the Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South won the Ford of Berusen with a charge across the ice.
n.The League: League soldiers smashed Beoraidh's catapults and League saboteurs fired its towers. The Towerjacks and Wolves of War helped clear Morrow, and the League helped pay for Winter's Mantle. Sarvos was alarmed when the Grendel armada sailed from its waters.
n.The Marches: Marcher soldiers captured Beoraidh's towers, and bounders and yeofolk repelled the Jotun from Bregasland. The Strong Reeds anchored the defence of Segura, while the Tusks and Drakes fought honourably in Stark.
n.Thule: Five Thule armies, nearly thirty thousand orcs under Grand Warlock Fljajokull, fought beside the Empire to clear Ossium and caused most of the Druj deaths. The Shard of Winter mysteriously broke ranks to destroy a fleeing Druj column.
n.Urizen: Caeli and Peregro were liberated and the Citadel Guard no longer declines, while thousands were rescued from Zenith, including 250 sentinels who joined the Citadel Guard. In Spiral, however, the Druj took Ossuary, Screed and the Legacy and threaten Apulian.
n.Varushka: Ossium, now Varushkan, was fully cleared of Druj with the Golden Axe and the Thule, and settlers are moving in from Karsk. The Northern Eagle and Iron Helms fought in Morrow, and Varushkan warriors guarded the saboteurs at Beoraidh.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark soldiers smashed Beoraidh's catapults. The Green Shield, Fist of the Mountain and Bloodcloaks retook Atalaq and Sealtoq and broke through at the Ford of Berusen, fighting honourably. Debate over Suaq who swore oaths as Jotun thralls bred some dissension in the ranks.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: its noble houses and villages are said to support Dawnish champions who fought the vallorn in Brocéliande.
t.Bay of Catazar: The Imperial armada gathered and sailed across the bay to Beoraidh and back, while the Grendel armada left its anchorage off Sarvos to strike Feroz.
t.Bregasland: Jotun pursuing the survivors of Bonering out of Liathaven were met by Marcher bounders and yeofolk and fell back across the border.
t.Brocéliande: Navarr, Dawnish knights, Highborn congregations and Tharim's servants held back the vallorn and saved the Broch. The miasma is thickening and larger horrors are emerging, however.
t.Feroz: The Grendel conquered the Cazar Straits and Oranseri and are three-tenths of the way to taking Fontargenta. Their pillaging will cost characters based there production next season.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: a Druj column fleeing Ossium towards it was destroyed by the Shard of Winter.
t.Hercynia: Tharim's servants are devouring its forests and herb gardens, which lose a rank of production for a year in exchange for his aid in Brocéliande.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun army that struck West Ranging crossed the border from Hordalant.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: settlers and wagon raiders are travelling east from Karsk into newly Varushkan Ossium.
t.Liathaven: The Bear Who Swims has nearly conquered West Ranging, ending Navarr hopes of driving the vallorn from the Westwood, while the Feni roam the northern woods.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: there were fears the departing Grendel armada would strike Trivento and the Spider's Dream, but it sailed on.
t.Mareave: The Imperial raid destroyed the Grendel fortification and coliseum at Beoraidh, so the Broken Shore orcs cannot raise an army here for a year.
t.Miaren: Its forests and herb gardens are being devoured by Tharim's servants, losing a rank of production for a year to pay for his aid in Brocéliande.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes' general promised to return the Jotun dead in cloths of Mitwold linen.
t.Morrow: The Druj fled and the Empire retook Caeli and Peregro unopposed, rooting out stragglers. Some spires had been left empty by massacre or by the gift of Kaela.
t.Necropolis: The Beoraidh raid launched from its overstretched quaysides, and the freed orcs returned here before heading north to Skarsind.
t.Ossium: Imperial and Thule forces took Nearweald and the Drownbark Forest, including Orieb. The whole territory apart from the Thule-held Bonewood is now Imperial.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: it is the homeland of the Thule armies that fought in Ossium, said to have few woodlands.
t.Redoubt: Its quaysides launched the Beoraidh raid and received the returning armada, and rescuers struck into Zenith from here and brought refugees back.
t.Sarvos: The Grendel armada anchored offshore set sail, causing panic before it headed south-west. Ships from Oran later brought refugees to its docks.
t.Segura: The Quiet Step and Strong Reeds held the Lasambrian Jotun in Anozeseri. Subtle Autumn magic thwarted the Corazón raids, though it fades with the Equinox.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: its nobles have ties to Boar's Dell and support Dawnish champions who fought in Brocéliande.
t.Sermersuaq: The Empire retook Atalaq and Sealtoq and pushed four-tenths of the way into Stark, where the new Jotun castle will make further progress harder.
t.Skarsind: The Winter Sun returned home, and about 2,500 freed orc warriors, plus others, are settling here to begin new lives as Imperial Orcs.
t.Spiral: A huge Druj army took Ossuary, Screed and the Legacy and nearly reclaimed Apulus. They have so far left the Block and the new heliopticon alone, and are cursing the territory with Spring magic.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: some Druj fleeing Nearweald retreated south into Farweald.
t.Therunin: Tharim is feasting on its forests and herb gardens, which lose a rank of production for a year in return for his support in Brocéliande.
t.Tsirku: Mentioned in passing: harsh winds blowing down from Tsirku brought hail and snow to Sermersuaq.
t.Zenith: The Druj still control the whole territory, but a three-month rescue raid freed two-thirds of the trapped Urizen, including soldiers who rejoined the armies.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Bone-armoured knights of Tharim fought here alongside Navarr and Dawnish defenders, and the region was saved from the vallorn.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Tharim's baron Poena led bound dead in its defence, and the Broch's survival kept the vallorn from surging into Elerael.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Grendel overran Cazar and Shantarim, looted the corsair families and enslaved many, and seized the Broken Shore Bounty office. A conjunction to the Pillars of the Osseini is on offer.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Bramar fell in a day and its wines were plundered. Most of the region remains Imperial, but the Grendel are three-tenths of the way to taking it.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Joharra and Oran fell, Lord Rahab rules from the Scorrero Nets office, and Imperial refugees are trapped inside the Asavean temple of Balo.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: The Bear Who Swims is nine-tenths of the way to conquering the region and camps at Silent Stand, which is offered as a Sentinel Gate conjunction.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: The Jotun advance likely ends Navarr hopes of uprooting the vallorn here before the Summer Solstice.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Imperial forces burned the nearly complete castle and the coliseum, freed thousands of slaves, and caught a Tarquinius ship trading granite and slaves.
r.Morrow/Altis: Mentioned in passing: giant hounds summoned into its hills ranged across Morrow hunting the Druj.
r.Morrow/Caeli: Liberated by the Citadel Guard and its allies, with new heliopticon towers, including a central replacement, being raised.
r.Morrow/Operus: Mentioned in passing: the Druj had already been denied their foothold here before the Winter Solstice.
r.Morrow/Peregro: Its spires were liberated, though at the Spire of the Red Sun the Druj killed as many captives as they could.
r.Necropolis/Hedrossan: Mentioned in passing: the Beoraidh raid departed from Necropolis's quaysides and returned there.
r.Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand: Mentioned in passing: Sanctuary was among the ports straining to launch the armada.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish armies advanced east from Bittershore.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Mentioned in passing: the Thule armies marched south from their domain in the Bonewood, which remains theirs.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Taken by the allies after Orieb and its serpent-carved palace fell. Here the Shard of Winter cut down a fleeing Druj column, aided by mysterious hooded Druj.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: Mentioned in passing: the allied pincer advanced south from Galath Fields.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: It fell first to the allied pincer, its abandoned settlements full of traps, and fleeing Druj scattered south and east.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt's quaysides launched the Beoraidh raid and welcomed back the armada and Zenith refugees.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt's ports launched the armada and received rescued Urizen from Zenith.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel armada anchored off Sarvos set sail, causing alarm on the quaysides.
r.Sarvos/Foracci: Mentioned in passing: frightened people fled north to Foracci when the Grendel armada stirred.
r.Segura/Anduzjasse: It remains wholly Lasambrian Jotun, and their forces rallied around Anduz and the Golden Terraces at season's end.
r.Segura/Anozeseri: Most of the fighting took place here, with a command post at Anozel. The Jotun foothold neither grew nor shrank.
r.Segura/Burnish: Mentioned in passing: losing its Tower of Anduz would cost the entire great work's benefit.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial armies could not defend Segura from here and moved south-west.
r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: The Lasambrians burned the ancient Sobral Stand, revealing a recently broken burial mound with smashed spiral-carved stones.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: Mentioned in passing: losing its Tower of Anduz would cost the entire great work's benefit.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Atalaq was retaken intact and Sealtoq liberated, but Suaq who swore thrall oaths face shame and division.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The Empire won the Ford of Berusen after the Freeborn charged across the frozen Atkonaroq and is four-tenths of the way to taking Stark. The new Tusks of the Lion castle now bars further progress.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: There was talk of pushing here instead, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction to Lansipari Head, a hub of thrall supply activity, is offered.
r.Spiral/Ankra: The new central heliopticon tower in southern Ankra is effectively complete, and the Druj have not interfered with it.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Ten thousand Druj retook almost all the liberated land and are halfway to claiming the region, camped miles from Apulian.
r.Spiral/Cinion: The Block here is effectively complete, though Druj scouts have watched it without attacking.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: The Druj took the region and the Legacy mithril mine, and a conjunction along the Twilight Way through Ossuary is offered.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Druj seized the Black Plateau, suffering its madness, and are working Spring curses on the territory there.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: Mentioned in passing: some Druj fleeing Nearweald retreated south into Farweald.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Spire Calator has become a Druj weapon-forge and dragonbone work-camp; some slaves were freed, but the spire was too well defended to attack.
r.Zenith/Lustri: Druj magic makes its forests hostile, but Spring and Night heralds aided fugitives, and only the bravest raiders went this deep.
r.Zenith/Occursion: Only the bravest warbands ventured here, finding fewer Druj and captives but long escape routes to safety.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The Druj retreated from Morrow along the trods into Proceris. There Highborn, Dawnish and Urizen raiders freed a camp of captured Highborn soldiers from its marsh farms.

A strange land.d: The Varushkan egregore made steady progress in Ossium, especially among the Ketsov, who erased Bone Scorpion symbols and sought Varushkan ways. They feared a Druj return and the loss of their weapons trade, so they proposed walls, a barracks and a Trading Exchange, which the Thule offered to build if the Empire would not. The Sand Fishers' coastal lands could support Varushkan settlers and help towards a fourth army. Options were to cede Misericorde, move them to Skarsind, or let the Thule offer sanctuary in Sküld. Dawnish and Varushkan statements opened opportunities for mandates. The Senate ceded Misericorde and the Pride assembly mandated preaching in Ossium. The other opportunities lapsed by Winter 383YE.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish National Assembly urged troubadours to bring tales of glory to Ossium, opening the opportunity for a mandate sending Dawnish knights to hunt the Druj miasma pillars. The civil service judged that the Ketsov and Sand Fishers had little interest in glory.
n.Druj: The Druj were in retreat but still contested Ossium, were expected to try to retake it within a year or two, and had left miasma pillars poisoning the land with dread.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: veterans of the Reikos campaign are said to remember the Druj miasma pillars well.
n.Imperial Orcs: Moving the Sand Fishers to Skarsind was considered, but they would add nothing to Imperial Orc strength or taxes, and ceding any region would disrupt the orcs living there.
n.The League: The Senate ceded Misericorde in Holberg to the Sand Fishers, so the region was no longer part of the League. In return Holberg's merchants were expected to profit from trade in fish, hides and timber.
n.Thule: The Thule offered to build and run the Ketsov Trading Exchange if the Empire would not. They also offered sanctuary in Sküld to the Sand Fishers and other Ossium orcs, but said they would approach them only with Senate or ambassadorial permission.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not discussed; the only related reference is a production table for Knightly Redoubts.
n.Varushka: Varushka received Ossium, where its egregore sought new citizens among the receptive Ketsov. The barracks and coastal resettlement were offered as a path to a fourth Varushkan army, and the Varushkan Assembly welcomed the Dawnish troubadours.

t.Holberg: Holberg lost its region of Misericorde, ceded to the Sand Fishers, with the trade they would bring expected to raise the territory's taxation by 8 thrones by year's end.
t.Ossium: Ossium's Ketsov embraced Varushkan ways and proposed walls, a barracks and a Trading Exchange. Its Crawling Depths mines could be upgraded to double mithril output, and the Pride assembly mandated preaching the Way to its people.
t.Otkodov: The Thule proposed resettling the Sand Fishers and other Ossium orcs in Otkodov's region of Sküld, as part of the Thule nation.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the territory itself is not discussed; 'Knightly Redoubts' appear only as an item in a production table.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Reikos campaign is recalled as the Empire's earlier encounter with Druj miasma pillars.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was considered as a new home for the Sand Fishers, but they would struggle in its harsh mountains, ceding land would disrupt its Imperial Orcs, and a region next to Crows Ridge would fall outside the Thule pacts.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Senate ceded Misericorde, a bandit-haunted forest with few citizens, to the Sand Fishers, who were expected to thrive on its marshy Semmerlak coast and possibly aid magistrates hunting fugitives there.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: The Thule offered homes on the banks of the Luhguren in Sküld to the Sand Fishers and other Ossium orcs, who would join the Thule nation.

Alter the works of Almodin Oktístis.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Redoubt, the motion targeted the Pallas Docks and Runeforge in Redoubt, Lorenzo's Great Game and Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty in Temeschwar, Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition in Tassato and Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance in Hahnmark. Its text gave a cost of six Senate commissions and either 92 thrones 4 crowns or 185 thrones, depending on Synod decisions. Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar provided the 92 thrones and 4 crowns after the Spring Equinox. The Great Game, the three Legacies, the Pallas Docks and the Spiral Sword were all to have their heretical elements removed. This worked alongside Synod Mandate 14: Synod-inspired mobs tore out the idolatrous statues and decorations as a message to the Asaveans, then Senate-employed craftspeople repaired the damage.

n.Grendel: The Spiral Sword was listed among the Oktístis works that would have their heretical elements removed.
n.The League: The League drove the motion: Temeschwar's senator proposed it, Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar paid the full cost, and three League works were cleansed of heretical elements.
n.Urizen: Redoubt's senator seconded the motion, and the Urizen works at Redoubt, including the Pallas Docks, were to be stripped of their heretical elements.
n.Wintermark: Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance, standing in Wintermark's Hahnmark, was among the works to have its heretical elements removed.

t.Hahnmark: Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance in Hahnmark was to have its heretical elements removed.
t.Redoubt: The motion named the Pallas Docks and the Runeforge in Redoubt, and the outcome confirmed that the Pallas Docks would lose their heretical elements.
t.Spiral: The Spiral Sword appears in the outcome among the works whose heretical elements would be removed.
t.Tassato: Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition in Tassato was to have its heretical elements removed.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's senator proposed the motion, a Temeschwar noble funded it, and Lorenzo's Great Game and Legacy of Loyalty there were to be cleansed of their heretical elements.

An affirming flame.d: Urizen's national assembly thanked the generals of the League, Highguard and Varushka. Narses, a refugee from Zenith, worked with Zakalwe to propose a library in Tassato Regario, or a larger Barossa School of Imperial Strategy, to house Zakalwe's quill. Either commission would need a Senate motion and would supply Prismatic Ink to one or both League generals. Furia Severia called in Adamant's favour so that koboldi would carve three giant Highborn soldiers from the Three Sorrows near the Weave, and this was done. Aurum consecrated the shrine with true liao. Varushka received no thanks because the Iron Helms had awakened the Black Plateau. A second statement explained that orcs could join Urizen only as an entire like-minded population.

n.Druj: The Druj had taken Zenith, spread a miasma there and invaded Morrow before being driven from the Caeli hills, and Menos holds that they could never be bonded to the Urizen nation.
n.Grendel: The Black Plateau killed Grendel soldiers on a horrifying scale and broke their armies in Spiral, though they are expected to rebuild. The blight may deter them from invading again, and they could never be bonded to Urizen.
n.Highguard: Highguard's three armies were honoured for three seasons of costly rearguard fighting in Zenith that let countless Urizeni escape. The Three Watchers now stand in their memory and are expected to draw Highborn pilgrims.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were cited as proof that orcs can choose a different path, having been taught to read by Urizeni teachers. Their own gregarious, martial culture means they are not seen as suitable candidates to join Urizen.
n.The League: The League generals Natalia and Gabriel Barossa were praised for helping turn back the Druj in Morrow. A proposed library or school in Tassato Regario would reward them with Prismatic Ink if the Senate commissioned it.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the slaughter caused by the Black Plateau was compared, uneasily, with what happened in the Mournwold.
n.Urizen: The Urizeni honoured their allies with a monument to the Highborn and a proposed gift for the League generals, but remained divided over Varushka's role. They also learned that orcs could join the nation only as a whole like-minded population.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle was credited for its role in Morrow, but the Iron Helms' awakening of the Black Plateau killed thousands of Imperial soldiers and Urizeni and left Spiral blighted. As a result, Urizen would not unite in thanking Varushka.

t.Morrow: Morrow was saved from collapse when League, Varushkan and Urizen forces drove the Druj back. The Three Watchers were carved near the Weave, overlooking a pass to Zenith.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: its suffering was compared with the slaughter caused by the Black Plateau, though its people reacted differently.
t.Spiral: Spiral remains blighted by the awakened Black Plateau and may not recover for decades. The Block keeps its connected spires habitable, but those outside them suffer, and some blame Varushka.
t.Tassato: Tassato was proposed as the site of a Library or School of Imperial Strategy honouring the League generals, subject to a Senate motion.
t.Zenith: Zenith, lost to the Druj, suffers under their miasma. Highborn armies were overwhelmed there while covering the flight of Urizeni citizens.

r.Morrow/Caeli: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were driven out of the Caeli hills during the Winter Solstice.
r.Morrow/Operus: Furia Severia's spire, the Weave, is in Operus, and her koboldi carved the Three Watchers into the Three Sorrows nearby. The shrine at the base of the central statue was consecrated with true liao.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: Tassato Regario was proposed as the home of a library or school, built with Zakalwe's quill, that would provide Prismatic Ink to the League generals.
r.Zenith/Occursion: The Spire of the Silver Chimera, a school of military study guarding a high pass in Occursion, burned when the Druj captured the region. Narses saved Zakalwe's quill from it.

Appoint Ambassador to Otkodov Spring 383.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by the senator for Karov, called for the election of an Ambassador to Otkodov. The page records only the outcome: Yevgeni Katzev, who already held the position, was reappointed. It gives no further details about the ambassador's duties or about how the vote went.

n.Thule: Thule's senators for Miekarova and Karov proposed and seconded the motion, which kept Yevgeni Katzev in place as Ambassador to Otkodov, a Thule territory.

t.Otkodov: Otkodov kept its incumbent ambassador, Yevgeni Katzev, who was reappointed to the post.

Appraisal of integration of Mournwold Or.d: Proposed by the Senator for Mournwold and seconded by the Senator for Sarvos, the motion asked the civil service to appraise how the Mournwold Orcs might be integrated into the Marches. Only one appraisal may be carried out each season. The motion passed, and the civil service was to deliver its report to the Empire before the Summer Solstice 383YE. The Speaker noted that this was the second motion the Senator for Sarvos had seconded at that Equinox, and the matter was passed to the magistrates as a possible case of subverting the agencies of state.

n.The Marches: The appraisal examines how the orc thralls of the Mournwold might be brought into the Marcher nation, with findings due before the Summer Solstice.

t.Mournwold: Mournwold's senator proposed the appraisal, which focuses on the future of the territory's orc thralls and their integration into the Marches.

Cede region of Misericorde to Sand Fishe.d: The motion ceded the Holberg region of Misericorde to the Sand Fishers, an orc nation in Ossium. It was proposed by the senator for Holberg, seconded by the senator for Karsk, and passed. As a result the region was ceded and the Sand Fishers settled there. The page notes that overall tax revenue for the territory of Holberg would rise by 8 thrones by the end of 383YE as a consequence of the arrangement.

n.The League: The League gave up direct control of Misericorde to the Sand Fishers at the proposal of Holberg's own senator, gaining a promised increase of 8 thrones in Holberg's tax revenue by the end of 383YE.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Karsk's senator seconded the motion, and the Sand Fishers are described as an orc nation in the Varushkan territory of Ossium.

t.Holberg: One of Holberg's regions was handed to the Sand Fishers, with the territory's overall tax revenue set to rise by 8 thrones by the end of 383YE.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is identified as the home of the Sand Fishers, the orc nation receiving Misericorde.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Misericorde was ceded outright to the Sand Fishers, who settled the region.

Chaos, and the stillness of it.d: The force needed to stop the vallorn doubled again. Military units could take the Slow the Vallorn action, paid in herbs by the Navarr. With 10,000 strength the Broch would survive another season. With 8,000 both regions would hold but the Broch would fall, though its people could escape. With 4,000 only Boar's Dell would hold, and below that the vallorn would claim about half of each region. Armies sent to Boar's Dell (via Semmerholm) or Elerael (via Reikos) could add up to 5,000 each. Highborn congregations, the Great Forest orcs and Tharim kept up their aid. Zakalwe gave a Find the Best Path boon to the Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield, and Llofir withdrew his offer.

n.Dawn: At Ranae de Rondell's urging Dawnish knights went to the greenwood, and Dawnish military units continued to receive additional rewards for fighting the vallorn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Druj presence made a route into Boar's Dell through Drycastle far less feasible, and the Great Forest orcs feared Druj malice while away.
n.Highguard: Highborn congregations answered Josephine of Adina's Charge with at least 500 strength. Tharim offered to add 2,000 force if allowed to feed on Highguard's herb gardens and forests.
n.Imperial Orcs: The opening story follows two Imperial Orc soldiers sent by Ziek to hold the wall beside the Navarr, one of them sickened by the vallorn and urged to seek bladeroot treatment.
n.Jotun: A significant Jotun force invaded Liathaven, threatening the Imperial foothold in West Ranging and making any reclamation of Westwood far harder.
n.Navarr: The Navarr faced a vallorn that doubled in strength again, threatening the Broch, Boar's Dell and Elerael. Their steadings paid defenders in herbs while Tharim's feeding withered herb gardens in three Navarr territories.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe suggested moving an army into Sermersuaq to free the Black Thorns, and the Kallavesi mystic Tremont of Cundahl took back his projections.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the nobles and yeofolk of Astolat continued to cheer those seeking glory against the vallorn.
t.Brocéliande: The vallorn heart in Brocéliande grew stronger again, and the fate of Boar's Dell, Elerael and the Broch hung on how much military strength the Empire committed.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: some Feni of Southridge had joined the Woods-that-Fell band that raided Hercynia.
t.Hercynia: Tharim's black frost withered Hercynia's herb gardens, and the Feni raiders who had stolen food, supplies and crystal mana there abruptly vanished.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Tremont of Cundahl was presumed to have returned home to Kallavesa with his reclaimed arcane projections.
t.Liathaven: The Jotun invaded Liathaven while time ran short to exploit its vallorn, and the eternal Surut would not help because the Conclave had not granted him amity.
t.Miaren: Tharim's black frost struck Miaren's herb gardens and forests as payment for his 1,000 strength against the vallorn.
t.Reikos: Reikos was almost certainly the only practical route for an army to reach Elerael without fighting through aggressive vallorn.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm offered the only safe route for an army to reach Boar's Dell, and its nobles and yeofolk continued to cheer Dawnish volunteers.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe suggested using Find the Best Path to move an army into Sermersuaq so the Black Thorns could go to Brocéliande.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, though Druj presence was cited as making the Drycastle route to Boar's Dell much less feasible.
t.Therunin: Therunin's herb gardens suffered Tharim's black frost, and its Senator Cybi Farkas brought about 1,000 Great Forest orcs to fight the vallorn.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Boar's Dell could be held with at least 4,000 strength or an army there; below that the vallorn would claim roughly half the region.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Elerael needed at least 8,000 strength or an army arriving via Reikos; otherwise the vallorn would push into it.
r.Hahnmark/Southridge: Mentioned in passing: Feni of Southridge had swollen the ranks of the band that raided Hercynia.
r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: There was speculation that the vanished Feni might have gone into Deer's Folly, the vallorn heart of Hercynia, though surely not by accident.
r.Hercynia/Old Ranging: The Feni raiders retreated into the deepest woods of northern Old Ranging and then disappeared, and Navarr scouts found no sign of them.
r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though Tremont of Cundahl was said to have returned to his home in Kallavesa.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: The Jotun invasion threatened the Imperial foothold in West Ranging, which the Empire would need to conquer in a single season against orc opposition.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: With a significant Jotun force in Liathaven, any attempt to reclaim Westwood from the vallorn became even more difficult.

Concede territory of Segura to Lasambria.d: The motion, proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Feroz, called for the Empire to concede the territory of Segura to the four tribes of the Lasambrian Jotun. It was put before the Senate in Spring 383YE and failed, so no concession of Segura was made. The page records no further details of the debate or the reasons for the motion's defeat.

n.Jotun: The four tribes of the Lasambrian Jotun would have received Segura had the motion passed, but its failure meant the Empire made no concession of the territory to them.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast faced a proposal to give up one of its territories, Segura, to the Lasambrian Jotun, but the motion's failure left the Empire's claim to it unconceded.

t.Segura: Segura was the subject of a proposed concession to the Lasambrian Jotun, which the Senate did not pass.

Conduit to destiny.d: A runeforge needed 60 wains of mithril, white granite and weirwood, 45 thrones and a year's work. Building it at Runegrott offered savings. If the Imperial Orcs returned the Gildenheim ruins in Skarsind and the Senate confirmed Wintermark's runesmiths as heirs, moving them would cost 12 thrones but save 30 wains of white granite and 60 crowns. Runesmiths enslaved by the Thule in 373YE might be ransomed. Hallowing Isenbrad's tomb with true liao would bring fifteen wains of weirwood. Recovering the lost Rime Hammer would see Runegrott fund the labour. Barien offered ice-walkers a Summer challenge. The Gildenheim ruins were moved to Runegrott in 383YE.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish weavers at work in Weirwater are cited as a famous example of Imperial magic.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Spiral Sword is named as the runeforge a new Wintermark forge would aim to rival.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Sentinel's Tomb in Casinea is cited as a precedent for an inspirational tomb having effects across the Empire.
n.Imperial Orcs: As owners of Skarsind, the Imperial Orcs held the Gildenheim runeforge ruins and could return them to Wintermark, having already refused significant Thule offers to buy them.
n.Thule: The Thule were believed to still hold the runesmiths and artisans enslaved at Gildenheim in 373YE, and had said they would return them only if paid what they were worth.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark was given a path to rebuild its runesmithing tradition with a new runeforge at Runegrott, possibly paired with a Runesmith title advising the Thane's Council, and the Gildenheim ruins were moved there to cut the cost.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the creation of the Sentinel's Tomb here is cited as the model for the wider inspiration an Isenbrad tomb might bring.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's Runegrott was proposed as the site of a new runeforge, a possible hallowed tomb to Isenbrad, and the home of the lost Rime Hammer, and it received the dismantled Gildenheim runeforge in 383YE.
t.Otkodov: The runesmiths captured at Gildenheim were taken to Otkodov and are likely still kept as slaves serving its undying masters.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind held the ruins of the Gildenheim runeforge, conquered by the Thule in 373YE, which were dismantled and moved out of the territory to Runegrott in 383YE.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Spiral Sword runeforge is named as the forge a new Wintermark runeforge would rival.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish weavers of Weirwater are cited as an example of the Empire's renowned magic.

r.Hahnmark/Northspires: The Runegrott ice caves beneath Northspires, guarded by runesmiths and the Eyes of the North, became the destination of the Gildenheim ruins and the proposed home of a new runeforge and a tomb to Isenbrad.

Construct Basilica of the Seven Doors.d: Proposed by the senator for Casinea and seconded by the senator for Bastion, the motion commissioned the restoration of the Basilica of the Seven Doors as a sinecure. The project used non-standard costs: 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns in labour, taking three months to complete. Thanks to the Custodes Clavium it needed no civil service commission slot and was entirely self-funded. Bartimaeus supplied the granite and weirwood after the Spring Equinox, and the Custodes Clavium met the labour costs. The restoration re-created the title Speaker of the Highborn Assembly, granting a congregation to its holder, who is appointed by the Highborn National Assembly at the Winter Solstice.

n.Highguard: Highguard gained a restored Basilica of the Seven Doors and a new national title, the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly, chosen by the Highborn National Assembly at the Winter Solstice and holding a congregation; the work was funded by the Custodes Clavium and the Benefactors of Highguard.

t.Bastion: The Basilica of the Seven Doors was restored in Bastion, with Bastion's senator seconding the motion and the construction taking three months to complete.

Construct Cinderpath Exchange II.d: Proposed by the senator for Bastion and seconded by the senator for Miekarova, the motion sought to commission the Cinderpath Exchange as a ministry in Mareholm, Casinea. The project drew on an opportunity presented by the benefactors of Highguard. It would have cost White Granite, been self-funded, and created the title 'Cinderpath Benefactor', to be appointed once a year by a vote of the congregation leaders of Highguard. The motion followed an earlier, unsuccessful attempt to build the same ministry, and this second motion also failed, so the Exchange was not commissioned.

n.Highguard: The Highborn missed a second chance to secure a ministry built on an opportunity from their own benefactors, along with a new title that their congregation leaders would have appointed each year.

t.Casinea: The Highguard territory of Casinea would have gained a new ministry, but the motion failed and no construction was commissioned.

r.Casinea/Mareholm: Mareholm was the proposed site of the Cinderpath Exchange, but it remained unbuilt after this second motion also failed.

Construct Cinderpath Exchange III.d: Issachar of the Unbound, proxy to Caleb of Reumah's Redoubt and bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction of the Cinderpath Exchange, drawing on an opportunity offered by the benefactors of Highguard. The ministry used non-standard costs: 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns in labour, with three months to construct. It was self-funded, and Rhesa provided the materials and money after the Spring Equinox 383YE. When complete, it will create a Highguard national position, the Cinderpath Custodian, chosen as a bourse position by Highborn owners of congregations, a method adopted on advice from the Constitutional Court.

n.Highguard: Highguard gains a white granite ministry and a new national title, the Cinderpath Custodian, chosen by Highborn congregation owners once construction is complete.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named; the only link is the word Redoubt in the proposer's title, Caleb of Reumah's Redoubt.

t.Casinea: The Cinderpath Exchange is being built in Casinea, with materials supplied and three months set for its completion.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not involved; Redoubt appears only in the name Caleb of Reumah's Redoubt.

r.Casinea/Mareholm: Mareholm is the site of the new Cinderpath Exchange ministry, funded with 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns provided by Rhesa.

Construct Hyljehal.d: Proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by the senator for Kallavesa, the motion commissioned a highly effective mana ministry on Rikkivesi as thanks to the Hylje for their help in the war with the Jotun. The title of Mediator of the Hyljehal is to be appointed by the Wintermark senators, bearing in mind the Hylje's request for a Suaq mediator in good standing. The commission used non-standard costs of 12 wains of weirwood and 24 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. Hengest Dunn provided the weirwood and crowns after the Spring Equinox, and on completion the ministry creates the Mediator title.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the hall is described as thanks to the Hylje for their help in the war against the Jotun.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark senators proposed and seconded the motion and will appoint the Mediator of the Hyljehal, with the Hylje asking for a Suaq mediator in good standing.

t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's senator seconded the motion, and the new floating hall is to be built on Rikkivesi, within the territory.

r.Kallavesa/Skymark: The Hylje floating hall, a mana ministry, is to be constructed on the lake of Rikkivesi in Skymark, with its materials funded after the Spring Equinox.

Construct Invisible Cord Brokerage.d: Proposed by the senator for Miaren and seconded by Temeschwar, the motion sought to commission a ministry in Seren drawing on an opportunity presented by the broker of Navarr. The ministry would have offered citizens the option of selling weirwood at a guaranteed price to a trusted broker, as an alternative to the fluctuating prices of the Public Bourse auction. It would have been a National Bourse position. The motion failed, so the Invisible Cord Brokerage was not constructed.

n.Navarr: Navarr's attempt to turn its broker's opportunity into a Navarr-controlled National Bourse ministry for weirwood failed, leaving the nation without the brokerage.

t.Miaren: Miaren's senator proposed building the weirwood ministry in Seren, but the motion failed and nothing was constructed there.

Construct Ketsov Trade Exchange.d: Announced in Spring 383YE under an Imperial Wayleave by Irina Vasileva Dukov, the ministry draws on an opportunity presented by the people of Ketsov and will allow the purchase of magical weapons and armour. It uses non-standard costs: 8 wains of white granite, 8 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov provided all the materials and crowns after the Spring Equinox. When complete, it will create the Imperial title Burgher of Ketsov, a Varushkan National Bourse position appointed annually by the votes of Varushkan mine and forest owners.

n.Varushka: Varushkan mine and forest owners will gain a new National Bourse title, the Burgher of Ketsov, chosen annually by their vote, and the full costs were met by Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov.

t.Ossium: A new trading exchange is to be built in the town of Ketsov in Ossium, offering magical weapons and armour for sale.

r.Ossium/Galath Fields: The Ketsov Trade Exchange ministry is to be constructed in Galath Fields over three months, drawing on an opportunity offered by the people of Ketsov.

Construct Pit of Revelations.d: Rather than a vote of the Senate, the project was commissioned through an announcement by a bearer of the Imperial Orc Wayleave, made by proxy for Skywise Laika. The Pit of Revelations is a mana sinecure built at standard cost: 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns in labour, taking three months to construct. After the Spring Equinox 383YE, Palerictus Krunk provided the full 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns. The sinecure creates a new Imperial title, the Marshal of the Pit of Revelations, to be held by whoever is appointed to oversee it.

n.Imperial Orcs: An Imperial Orc Wayleave bearer used their authority to commission the sinecure in their own homeland, giving the Empire a new mana-producing title rooted in Imperial Orc lands.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind gains a new mana sinecure, the Pit of Revelations, and with it the Imperial title of Marshal of the Pit of Revelations.

r.Skarsind/Skogei Glens: The Pit of Revelations is to be built in the south-west of Skogei Glens, with construction taking three months once the mithril and labour were provided.

Construct Root and Stem Apothecarium.d: In Spring 383YE the Senate approved construction of the Root and Stem Apothecarium in Meade, Mitwold, taking up a limited, self-funded opportunity. The project needed 8 wains of weirwood, 16 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Spring Equinox William Lowther supplied 4 wains of weirwood, and Will Talbot supplied a further 4 wains of weirwood and 2 Thrones. Once complete, the ministry will create a new Imperial title, the Master of the Root and Stem, to be appointed nationally by the Bourse.

n.The Marches: Marchers took the lead on the project, with their senators proposing and seconding it and Marcher donors supplying the weirwood. The resulting ministry brings a new Bourse-appointed title, the Master of the Root and Stem, into the nation's Bladeroot trade.

t.Mitwold: Mitwold is to gain a Kruidenkenner warehouse dedicated to the Bladeroot trade, built in its town of Meade at its own senator's proposal.

r.Mitwold/Meade March: The Root and Stem Apothecarium is to be built in the town of Meade, with three months of construction once the weirwood and labour costs are met.

Construct spy network in Ossium.d: Proposed by the senator for Karov and seconded by the senator for Ossium, the motion commissioned a spy network in Ossium named the Ossium Watchers. It carried standard costs of 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns in labour, took three months to build, and requires upkeep of 2 thrones per season. Vuk the Wolfeater provided the weirwood and crowns after the Spring Equinox 383YE, and the network was set to be constructed in Ossium.

n.Varushka: Varushka's senators for Karov and Ossium proposed and seconded the motion, giving the nation a new spy network watching over one of its own territories.

t.Ossium: Ossium was to gain the Ossium Watchers, a spy network built with weirwood and crowns supplied by Vuk the Wolfeater.

Double or nothingness.d: The Winter Solstice law made selling or gifting liao into the Confederacy by port or across the border a crime, but it appears to allow trade with Suranni inside the Empire. The Silent Bell reported to Cardinal of Vigilance Irada von Temeschwar a smuggling route, probably run by Imperial citizens from a stockaded camp, that takes liao from Feroz into Arbonne (Kalino) in exchange for silver, green iron and some mithril. Dumon's Hand proposed a concealed ministry in the south-west, trading liao for Winter vis; this would need Senate or other authorisation and risks a diplomatic incident. Susanna of the Seventh Star urged the Synod to invite Dumon's Hand to explain their beliefs, while Mitra the Uncompromising called for their condemnation and an inquisition of Palladius of Urizen.

n.Highguard: The Highborn priest Susanna of the Seventh Star proposed a General Assembly statement inviting Dumon's Hand to explain their beliefs, possibly at the White City or the Seminary of the Swan, and Casinea and Necropolis were floated as possible sites for the liao ministry.
n.The Brass Coast: The smuggling route uncovered by the Silent Bell runs from southern Feroz, and Kahraman and Madruga are among the places Dumon's Hand now favours for a proposed ministry trading liao for Winter vis.
n.The League: Tassato and Sarvos are among the sites Dumon's Hand suggested for a concealed ministry that would exchange liao for Winter vis, should the Empire commission it.
n.Urizen: The Urizeni illuminate Mitra the Uncompromising led priests demanding that Dumon's Hand be condemned as heretics and that Palladius of Urizen be called to inquisition for vindicating them.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the White City is suggested as a neutral place where Dumon's Hand representatives might meet priests of the Way.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: not named, though the new law bans liao reaching the Confederacy via ports.
t.Casinea: Casinea is named as a possible, more distant site for the proposed ministry trading liao to Dumon's Hand for Winter vis.
t.Feroz: The Silent Bell identified a smuggling route carrying large amounts of liao from southern Feroz across the border, and earlier suggestions to build the ministry there have been reconsidered.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman is one of the sites Dumon's Hand now favours for a disguised ministry exchanging liao for Winter vis, if one is commissioned.
t.Kalino: Known to the Suranni as Arbonne, Kalino is the destination of the liao smuggling route, with metals including silver, green iron and mithril flowing back into the Empire.
t.Madruga: Madruga is one of the sites suggested by Dumon's Hand for a concealed ministry trading liao for Winter vis.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: not named; the territory's only link is through Urizeni figures such as Palladius and Mitra.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis is named as a possible, more distant site for the proposed ministry trading liao to Dumon's Hand for Winter vis.
t.Reikos: The Seminary of the Swan in Reikos is suggested as a venue where Dumon's Hand might share their spiritual understanding with Imperial priests.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos is one of the sites Dumon's Hand suggested for a disguised ministry exchanging liao for Winter vis.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: south-east Segura was previously suggested as a ministry site, but this has been reconsidered given the new law and Suranni embargo.
t.Shavronne: Mentioned in passing: not named; it is affected only as part of the Iron Confederacy to which liao trade is now banned.
t.Tassato: Tassato is one of the sites Dumon's Hand suggested for a concealed ministry trading liao for Winter vis.

r.Morrow/Ravion: Mentioned in passing: Ravion is not named on the page.

Home fires.d: Friar John's statement, upheld 102-0 at the Winter Solstice 382YE, urged farm owners to feed and rest soldiers. Marchers judged a nightly meal impractical and instead proposed billeting whole armies across a territory's farms, with able soldiers working for their board. This would cut the cost of supporting the army by ten thrones per territory, in Bregasland, Upwold or Mitwold. Competing mandates would allow only Marcher armies or any Imperial army. After the Spring Equinox, Friar John enacted the version open to all Imperial armies. Other opportunities were also raised: extending the Breadbasket to the Mournwold, helping soldiers trade military units or fleets for farms, and building a fortification in Gravenmarch after Friar William's vigilance statement.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Friar William's statement named the Jotun as a threat Marchers should watch for, and the page notes they have never shown interest in Bregasland.
n.The Marches: Marcher farms can now billet Imperial armies, with able soldiers working the land in exchange for food and board. Not every Marcher welcomes the cost or the presence of outsiders on their land. Further proposals were offered to help soldiers settle as farmers and to fortify Bregasland.

t.Bregasland: An army can now be billeted across Bregasland's farms, reducing its support cost by ten thrones. As the only Marcher territory without a fortification, it was also offered the chance to build one in Gravenmarch.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold is one of the Marcher territories where a general may now billet an army on the farms, cutting the cost of supporting it by ten thrones.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold's less fertile farms lack access to the Imperial Breadbasket, so armies cannot be billeted there. That would change if the Breadbasket were extended to cover it, which remained an opportunity.
t.Upwold: Upwold is one of the Marcher territories where an army can now be dispersed across the farms, with soldiers working in exchange for bed and board.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Gravenmarch is the only part of marshy Bregasland suited to a standard fortification, and one could be built there to protect the territory. This was offered as an opportunity, not completed.

Honey and vinegar.d: Tassato merchants proposed expanding the mana exchanges of Tassato, Sarvos and Temeschwar (one commission, 60 wains of mithril, 120 crowns) to improve every grandmaster's ministry. Holberg's burghers offered a new exchange for the warmage or bursar, or a great exchange for both. Marcher landskeepers let farm owners diversify to produce mana while Rivers Run Red stays interdicted. Mournwold miners pledged a bequest to the Silver Chalice for a declaration against cursing citizens, and Landskeeper Shem brought a proposal to the Throne. Displaced hylje sought a floating Hyljehal with a Suaq mediator. The Senate later approved the grandmasters' expansion in Spring 384YE. The Holberg opportunity lapsed.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: their invasion of Sermersuaq has driven the hylje south, and the sealfolk hope to see the orcs driven back.
n.The League: League merchants offered to expand the exchanges of Tassato, Sarvos and Temeschwar to supply the grandmasters, a project the Senate approved in Spring 384YE. Holberg's burghers proposed their own exchange for the warmage or bursar, an opportunity that later lapsed.
n.The Marches: Grateful that Rivers Run Red stayed interdicted, the landskeepers let Marcher farm owners raise menhirs to produce mana, and sent Landskeeper Shem to Anvil with a proposal for the Imperatrix. Mournwold miners offered the Silver Chalice a bequest in return for a declaration against cursing Imperial citizens.
n.Wintermark: The hylje, crediting Wintermark for their recognition as a people, offered trade and mana through a floating Hyljehal on the Rikkivesi. It would have a Suaq merchant as Mediator, possibly as a Wintermark national title.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: hylje fleeing the Jotun have been seen in greater numbers on the northern lakes of Bruckland.
t.Holberg: Holberg, the only League city without a mana exchange, was offered one for the warmage or bursar, or a great exchange for both. The opportunity later lapsed.
t.Kallavesa: The hylje proposed mooring a floating Hall of the Hylje on the Rikkivesi. There they would trade fish, crabs, eels and lake-bed mana crystals with the Suaq.
t.Mournwold: Half a dozen Mournwold mine owners pledged green iron, weltsilver and tempest jade each season to the Silver Chalice if the Conclave declared that curses must never be used to slay Imperial citizens. Marcher farms here could also be diversified to produce mana.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos's mana exchange was one of three proposed for expansion to supply the grandmasters, a project the Senate approved in Spring 384YE.
t.Sermersuaq: Hylje driven from Sermersuaq by the Jotun invasion intend to return home once the fighting ends. Meanwhile they offered to support the Mark through trade.
t.Tassato: Tassato's merchants devised the plan to expand the three League exchanges, including their own, to sell surplus mana to the civil service. The Senate approved it in Spring 384YE.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's mana exchange was one of three proposed for expansion to supply the grandmasters, a project the Senate approved in Spring 384YE.

r.Hahnmark/Bruckland: Mentioned in passing: hylje displaced by the Jotun have been seen in greater numbers on Bruckland's northern lakes.

I heard a source.d: Ephisis offered to sell Autumn vis through a refurbished tower in Kalpaheim, needing 16 wains of mithril, 32 Crowns and a Senate commission or Wayleave. Pained by the Liberty Pact, the City wanted new Senate wayleaves as a sign of commitment to trade. Each one would allow a similar ministry for another realm at sites in Temeschwar, Meade, Seren, Siroc and Bastion. It refused an unlimited Ephisis' Scale. If the Senate relinquished every major Bourse seat and made them all Imperial, it promised Autumn vis trade everywhere and a strengthened Imperial regio. Prospero's herald urged the opposite, making every seat national, for matching benefits.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Spiral Castle is named as a lesser Bourse resource whose status would not matter under Ephisis' all-Imperial Bourse proposal.
n.Highguard: Ephisis' heralds identified Bastion as a site where a ministry could supply prismatic ink to the Empire, provided the Senate created an additional wayleave and commissioned the facility.
n.Navarr: Seren was named as a possible site for a ministry trading vital honey from the City of Gold and Lead, available only if the Senate created more wayleaves.
n.The Brass Coast: Siroc was put forward by Ephisis' heralds as a location for a ministry supplying crystal fire, should the Senate create an extra wayleave and commission it.
n.The League: Temeschwar was proposed as the site of a possible ministry trading heart's blood, depending on the Senate creating additional wayleaves.
n.The Marches: Meade was identified as a possible site for a ministry supplying golden apples, contingent on new wayleaves and a separate commission.
n.Wintermark: The Hidden Prince claimed the deeds to Ogila's unfinished, sealed runesmith tower on the street of runes in Kalpaheim. He proposed completing it as a mithril-doored trading post where heralds of Ephisis would sell Autumn vis.

t.Bastion: Bastion was named as a suitable location for a ministry providing prismatic ink, requiring a new wayleave, 16 wains of mithril and 32 Crowns.
t.Hahnmark: An abandoned tower in Kalpaheim, sealed since the runesmith Ogila's death, could be completed with mithril and fitted with doors for heralds of the City of Gold and Lead. Merchants would then sell Autumn vis there.
t.Madruga: Siroc was identified as a site where a ministry could supply crystal fire, if the Senate created a further wayleave and commissioned the facility.
t.Miaren: Seren was proposed as the location for a possible ministry providing vital honey through trade with Ephisis.
t.Mitwold: Meade was put forward as a site for a ministry supplying golden apples, available only alongside a new Senate wayleave.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral Castle is cited as a lesser Bourse resource excluded from Ephisis' requirement that all major Bourse seats be Imperial.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar was named as a suitable site for a ministry supplying heart's blood, should the Senate create an additional wayleave and commission it.

Idle hands are the devil's playthings.d: Almodin's Senate commissions were all decorated with effigies of Asavean gods. The Synod could fund a year-long blockade (100 liao) that would shut the Great Game, Pallas Docks, Runeforge and Lorenzo's Legacies. It could instead send a mob to tear down the idols (25 liao), wrecking the buildings and giving a year's boost to local congregations. A third option (50 liao) would follow Ivarsgard's example and repurpose the idols, giving a permanent boost. Chainbreaker Snark proposed a variant that would also storm the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz. Action against the Temple would hurt trade and anger Asavea. The Senate could also alter the commissions or revoke the Temple's permission.

n.Grendel: The Grendel currently hold a cordon around the Temple of the Black Bull in Feroz. Snark's proposed mandate would need a large mob to break through it, probably at the cost of Grendel and Imperial lives, and how the Grendel would respond is uncertain.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn would face lost taxes, lost orichalcum profits from trade with Nemoria and local unrest if the Temple in Feroz were blockaded or destroyed. Freeborn sutannir Franco i Erigo would lose his delegate's benefits, or the post entirely.
n.The League: The League holds several of Almodin's works: Lorenzo's Legacies in Temeschwar and Tassato and the Great Game. A League senator, Rafael Barossa di Tassato, raised the Pride Assembly's condemnation, and Holberg's Wunderkind guild designed the stelae that protesters could turn out of phase.
n.Urizen: The Runeforge in Redoubt is one of Almodin's buildings. Pilgrims in Redoubt could ring it in protest, and its idols could be torn down or repurposed, damaging it until it is repaired.
n.Varushka: Varushka had already led the way: the boyar of Ivarsgard had the idols at Lestasny ground into gravel, and Karsk's buildings were already defaced. Karsk congregations would gain double benefits for a year if a destruction mandate passed.
n.Wintermark: Veikko Bondforger's condemnation of the architect was echoed by the Pride Assembly. Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance in Hahnmark is among the works that could be shut down, defaced or repurposed.

t.Feroz: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull at Oran would be cordoned under the first mandate and destroyed under the others, costing trade and taxes and causing local unrest. Snark's variant would see a mob storm it and force its Asavean priests to recant or die.
t.Hahnmark: Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance stands here. Locals could turn its stelae out of phase to shut it down, or a mandate to remove its idols would damage it but swell local congregations.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's Wunderkind guild designed the adjustable red stone stelae used in Lorenzo's Legacies.
t.Karsk: Almodin's buildings in Karsk had already been defaced. Under either destruction mandate its congregations would gain four extra votes and two extra doses of liao for a year, for having led the Empire's response.
t.Redoubt: The Runeforge here could be ringed by protesting pilgrims and shut down. Alternatively it could be damaged by the removal of its idols, with Pride boosting local congregations.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Qanat commissioned in Segura was never begun and its motion has lapsed, so it needs no action.
t.Tassato: Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition here could be shut down by locals turning its stelae out of phase, or damaged and stripped of its idols under the other mandates.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar hosts Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty and the Great Game. Local pilgrims could blockade them, or have their idols torn down or repurposed, closing them until they are repaired.

r.Karsk/Lestasny: Almodin fortified Lestasny, but the boyar of Ivarsgard had its Asavean statues used to gravel the courtyard so Imperial boots tread on the false gods. This lasting act of defiance is held up as the model for the third mandate.

If the wheel is fixed.d: The Sumaah House of Courage narrowly passed a statement pausing missionary work in the Empire, so penalties on congregations along the Bay of Catazar ended for now. The House of the Way narrowly pledged no new paragons, exemplars or doctrine changes for a year. Laloc, pilgrim of Courage, set out five Sumaah concerns: unilateral doctrine changes, compromise with false faiths, the role of paragons and exemplars, differing views of the virtues, and the place of orcs in the Way. If the General Assembly passes a matching statement by the Summer Solstice, delegates will meet at Anvil. Otherwise the Sumaah will assume reconciliation is impossible. Meanwhile the Sumaah remain divided over orc virtue and still exterminate orcs.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: in the in-character exchange, Laloc remarks that the Empire's treatment of the Druj has not changed since they accepted the doctrine of the ancestors.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Bastion is set against Timoj as a rival heart of the Way, and the Sumaah Embassy in Necropolis serves as a point of diplomatic contact.
n.Imperial Orcs: The place of orcs in the Way is a central Sumaah grievance: they question the recognition of two orc exemplars and an orc cardinal and suggest the Empire may have been guilty of idolatry. The Sumaah still exterminate the orcs they encounter while their Houses remain divided over whether orcs can be virtuous.

t.Bastion: Bastion's standing as the heart of the Way is at stake: the mandate urged that it be seen as Timoj's equal, and the Sumaah want any reconciliation between Timoj and Bastion settled through talks.
t.Bay of Catazar: The penalties suffered by congregations along the Bay of Catazar from Sumaah missionary preaching have ended, at least for now.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Sumaah Embassy in Necropolis handles relations between the House of the People and the Senate, separate from Laloc's role for the Sumaah Synod.

Lost in translation.d: Skywise Tulva's Winter mandate invited the freed slaves to settle in Skarsind, but without provisions they set out at winter's end with little idea of the way. Progress was slow, and many survived only by the charity of Imperial citizens. The civil service judged that a motion would no longer help and that independent captains must track the refugees down. The more military strength committed, the more would reach Skarsind: 10,000 would bring all of them, while under 5,000 would bring fewer than a quarter and leave bandits on the frontiers. Help might also come from the Winter Sun, the Freedom-Heresy humans travelling with the Great Forest Orcs, or Irra Harah. Rewards could come from the guerdon or an Imperial Orc Synod mandate.

n.Dawn: Handfuls of refugees strayed as far as Astolat and Semmerholm, and those on outskirts such as Dawn were unlikely ever to be found unless a large search was mounted. Papa Otec also restated its intent to kill Semmerholm's senator Zadkiel de Coeurdefer.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj, with the Dawnish, crushed the Barrens, from which the Great Forest Orcs and their human companions fled.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the freed slaves were rescued from the Grendel in the raids on the Broken Shore.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highborn well-wishers were among those who donated food and resources to the refugees.
n.Imperial Orcs: The refugees were heading for an Imperial Orc homeland, and their arrival could give Imperial Orc businesses and farms extra production if enough were escorted there. The national assembly could also pass a mandate trading a season of reduced production for rewards to the captains who helped.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs were walking the trods in support of their Navarr allies, and could leave them to join the search.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast well-wishers donated supplies to the refugees, and a handful of them ended up as far astray as Kahraman. Papa Otec restated its intent to kill Feroz's senator Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza.
n.The League: League well-wishers donated to the refugees, and some orcs reached as far north as Temeschwar by following the Blood Red Roads.
n.Wintermark: A few refugees reached Kalpaheim, and the accompanying story follows a young Wintermark refugee from Solvi stealing food to feed starving orcs in the spirit of 'all that is worthwhile'.

t.Astolat: A handful of refugees ended up in Astolat, an out-of-the-way territory where they were unlikely to be found without a substantial search.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: many refugees were reduced to begging outside the villages and towns north of the Bay.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Papa Otec remained committed to the death of the senator for Feroz, Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the story's young narrator mourns his home city of Solvi, lost to the orcs.
t.Kahraman: A handful of refugees strayed as far as Kahraman, having underestimated the size of the Empire.
t.Semmerholm: A handful of refugees wandered into remote Semmerholm, and Papa Otec restated its intent to kill the territory's senator, Zadkiel de Coeurdefer.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was the refugees' intended new home, but only a handful had arrived by the Equinox. Whether the rest arrive, bringing a possible boost to Imperial Orc production, depended on how much military strength was committed to escorting them.
t.Temeschwar: A few refugees reached Temeschwar by following the Blood Red Roads northward.

Music of a distant drum.d: Angered that Liberty Pact tariffs were imposed without consultation, the Thule of Otkodov imposed their own and stopped Imperial harvesting of ambergelt and mana crystals in Krevsaty.
