Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-Undivided and Grand Warlock Fljajokull planned a delegation to the Senate to discuss tariffs and the ransom of nearly three thousand Imperial slaves, likely payable in weirwood, mithril and white granite. Snowstorm Henk's research expedition was detained in Otkodov near disputed Sungold Pass. The Great Forest Orcs proposed a weirwood embassy at Peakedge Stead. The Tsark spy network was discovered and is being dismantled. A Jotun delegation sought Wintermark's mediators, relations with the Mournwold thralls stagnated, and the Grendel took nearly half of Feroz.

n.Druj: Thule warbands in Ossium were rumoured to be taking captured Druj soldiers north into the Bonewood, and the Druj sent a grim new message shortly before the Equinox after Urizen rebuffed their peace overture.
n.Grendel: The Grendel armada conquered nearly half of Feroz while their pirates kept harassing Imperial merchant shipping, even as Imperial captains raided Beoraidh.
n.Highguard: The Great Forest Orcs, who value friends made in Reikos, said they would much prefer a Highborn or Navarr Ambassador to the Great Forest if the embassy were built.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc scholar Snowstorm Henk was detained by the Thule in Sküld, Bloodcrow Losak's statement urging outreach to the Mournwold thralls failed badly, and a Jotun delegation asked to observe the Imperial Orcs' Night of Worth.
n.Jotun: A delegation from Jarl Haska Whitemane, led by Arne Emblasbarn and Val Longarm, was coming to Anvil to discuss the destruction of the Meeting Place with Wintermark, while a third Jotun force moved into Liathaven.
n.Navarr: The Great Forest Orcs proposed a weirwood embassy at Peakedge Stead, preferring a Navarr or Highborn ambassador. Work began on the Holt of the Oak, and a Navarr magistrate was allowed to visit the detained Imperial scholars.
n.The Brass Coast: The Grendel armada conquered nearly half of Feroz, and the Empire continued to fight the Jotun in Segura.
n.The Marches: Mournwold Marchers stayed on relatively cordial terms with the former Jotun thralls, but tensions grew as the orcs spread further afield, stoked by agitator Bill Tavistock of Whittle.
n.Thule: Otkodov answered Imperial sanctions with tariffs of its own, closed Krevsaty's resources to Imperial harvesters, detained an Imperial expedition, kept its claim to Sungold Pass and sent a formal delegation to negotiate slave ransoms and tariffs.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen had soundly rebuffed the Druj's earlier peace overture.
n.Varushka: Varushkan Yevgeni Katzev served as ambassador to Otkodov, Sungold Pass in eastern Varushka stayed contested, and the Varushkans were due to choose the Gift of the Dwindling Star seat, whose ilium the Thule could withdraw.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's mediators were sought by a Jotun delegation that wanted to discuss the destruction of the Meeting Place with Wintermark rather than with the Empire.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Empire and the Grendel remained locked in a struggle for the bay, with pirates still harrying Imperial vessels and a proposal raised to take the fight to them.
t.Feroz: The Grendel armada conquered nearly half of Feroz.
t.Karsk: The Thule tightened border controls in Krevsaty, ended Imperial access to its ambergelt and mana crystals, and began building a fortification in its hills.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: a third force of western orcs was noted as having moved into Liathaven.
t.Mareave: Imperial ship captains completed a daring raid on Beoraidh, and the success raised Imperial morale.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: named with Skarsind as a place where ransomed Imperial slaves would be delivered.
t.Mountains of the Moon: The people of Tsark discovered the Imperial spy network and were systematically breaking up its caches and camps, with the network due to be fully dismantled by the Summer Solstice.
t.Mournwold: The former Jotun thralls lived relatively peacefully but grew more confident, and relations neither improved nor worsened amid calls both to embrace and to eject them.
t.Ossium: Thule forces aided the Empire in Ossium from the Bonewood, were rumoured to be taking Druj captives north, and sought Imperial approval before approaching the local orcs.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov held nearly three thousand Imperial slaves in its farms, mines and quarries, imposed retaliatory tariffs, and detained Imperial scholars accused of trespass, theft and espionage.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs meet friends from Reikos at Peakedge Stead.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the Empire continued to engage the Jotun in Segura.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Empire continued to engage the Jotun there, and Crow's Keep's watchtowers overlooked passes into its Silver Peaks.
t.Skarsind: Expansion of Crow's Keep, with watchtowers over passes into Urdur and the Silver Peaks, was expected to finish shortly before the Summer Solstice, and Skarsind was named as a delivery point for ransomed slaves.
t.Therunin: Work began on the Holt of the Oak with Navarr weirwood and donated funds, and the Great Forest Orcs offered to help build an embassy at Peakedge Stead.

r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Imperial harvesting of ambergelt from the Krevsaty Yelta and mana crystals from the Proritsatel Oloy was halted by the Thule, who had also begun a fortification in the hills.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Imperial ship captains completed a daring raid on Beoraidh.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: Matriarch Hamma the Lame, a respected thrall elder considered exceptionally wise, owns the Eversweet Orchard here and could be contacted by Winged Messenger.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Bill Tavistock of Whittle, an outspoken opponent of the former thralls, could be contacted here.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Hap the Soft, who takes in orc and human orphans and trains them as shepherds, lives at Golden Hoof Farm here.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Timber merchant Sigdór, thought to be an expert on the thrall religion, lives at Sigdór's Stead here.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Ritual magician Casta the Black, one of the thralls' respected figures, lives at the Circle of the Steel King here.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The Thule used the Bonewood as their base for aiding the Empire and were rumoured to be dragging captured Druj soldiers into its depths.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Snowstorm Henk and four companions were held in the Thule camp at Sküld, unharmed but not released.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Mentioned in passing: Crow's Keep's watchtowers and garrisons overlook the passes into Urdur.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: Crow's Keep's watchtowers overlook the passes into the Silver Peaks.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Mentioned in passing: noted as the primary home of the Great Forest Orcs.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: The Great Forest Orcs proposed an embassy at Peakedge Stead, built entirely of weirwood with their help, which would require a Senate motion.

One more day's light.d: A mutilated yeofolk, Ramsey, was released to carry a Druj ultimatum to Semmerholm. For every army attacking a Druj territory, one in ten Dawnish prisoners in Dawnguard would be killed, and the children held at Drycastle would lose their protection. Healed by a Dawnish witch, Ramsey reported that the children were kept in relative comfort while the adults were worked mercilessly. After the Conclave reconciled with Irra Harah and granted it amity, its agents, the Children of Papa Otec, prepared hidden routes for a mission of mercy. Military units, and possibly the Winter Sun or Seventh Wave, could support it, with rescues growing with strength. A Sentinel Gate strike on Dourfell Chase could bolster the effort.

n.Dawn: Dawn's captive people in Dawnguard faced Druj threats of torture and death for every Imperial attack. The foray offered a chance to free the children at Drycastle and up to two-fifths of those taken when Drycastle fell.
n.Druj: The Druj used hostages as leverage to deter invasion and grew crueller to their slaves. The proposed foray threatened their hold on prisoners, their watch on the Eaves of Peytaht and production at the Fangs mithril mine.
n.Highguard: The Seventh Wave could commit half its strength to the foray while defending an Imperial territory, gaining a detailed military report on the Barrens. Reikos would receive those rescued through the Forest of Peytaht.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun could support the foray instead of escorting the orcs. If a rebel band formed in the Barrens, the rebels would see the Imperial Orcs, and the Winter Sun's general especially, as allies.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: most orc slaves freed in a full-strength raid would be expected to join their Great Forest cousins in Navarr-held Therunin.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: hare-marked agents of Irra Harah were recalled as having aided refugees of the Mournwold a few years earlier.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the earlier Druj peace overture to the Urizen had been soundly rebuffed, and the Urizen are noted as knowing Druj oppression.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Druj message came after their armies retreated from Varushkan-held Ossium, which they said they would leave to the Empire for now.

t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: refugees of the Mournwold were among those once aided by Irra Harah's hare-marked friends.
t.Ossium: The last orc armies had withdrawn from Ossium, and the Druj declared they would allow the Empire and its allies to hold it for now.
t.Reikos: Reikos was a destination for rescued children, Dawnish slaves and freed orcs, who would be escorted there through the haunted Forest of Peytaht.
t.Semmerholm: Ramsey arrived in Semmerholm bearing the Druj ultimatum. A secret route from Semmerholm into Dawnguard would carry heroes in and bring rescued captives back to safety.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens was the target of the proposed covert mission of mercy, which at higher strengths would free thousands of slaves, disrupt Druj operations and possibly create a rebel sanctuary.
t.Therunin: At the highest level of support, most of the extra orc slaves freed would be expected to join their cousins in Therunin.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: refugees of Zenith were among those once aided by Irra Harah's hare-marked friends.

r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: With at least 15,000 strength, the foray could free slaves held in Bitter Strand.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: The Dawnish children held at Drycastle and the enslaved adults across Dawnguard were the foray's main objective, and the prisoners the Druj threatened to kill.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: With at least 10,000 strength, prisoners in the Heart of Peytaht could be freed, and the raid would disrupt the Eaves of Peytaht to secure 10 wains of weirwood.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: The Druj shun the ruins of Dourfell Keep. A Sentinel Gate strike on their watch-post at Dourfell Chase could boost the foray and, if Irra Harah claimed it, become a lasting sanctuary.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: With at least 10,000 strength, the foray could free prisoners held in Murderdale.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Mentioned in passing: the hidden routes might let particularly daring heroes reach people in need as far afield as Saltmarsh.
r.The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth: With at least 15,000 strength, slaves could be freed here and production at the Fangs mithril mine roughly halved for a year.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: Freed orcs who wished to stay and fight the Druj could find sanctuary in the Untrod Groves with Irra Harah's aid.

Point of the spear.d: In Sermersuaq, heroes could fight Jarl Heimgar to free about 50 captured Imperial soldiers, free Suaq thralls held at Thoki's Camp, or visit a broken Jotun warband in Suaq Font. Two Brocéliande skirmishes could each add 500 military strength against the vallorn. In Feroz, conjunctions targeted Kraken's Jaw beast masters and their sand crabs, and aimed to free islanders, Highguard pilgrims and stranded Imperial orc reavers. In Segura, heroes could protect Faraden trade. Other conjunctions offered to cleanse a Druj monolith in Ossium, intercept a Vikari warband in Spiral, find a League ship off Redoubt, stop Feni in the Marches, clear ghouls from a Karsk dragonbone forest and pursue the thieves of the Magistrate's Grasp in Casinea.

n.Dawn: Dawn's lands were where the trail began: travellers vanished in Coombe and bandits stole the Magistrate's Grasp. Astolat's militia then traced the hirers, The Harvesters, to Casinea.
n.Druj: A lingering Druj monolith spread fear over Sullen Vale in Ossium. A Druj warband of Vikari mages, Chikad warriors and slave artisans led by a young Ghulai was marching out of Screed and could be intercepted.
n.Grendel: Grendel forces in Feroz were targets of several conjunctions: Kraken's Jaw beast masters with sand crabs, a garrison on Ponta Delgordo, skirmishers on the Lucksprings Road and mercenaries at Green Coast. A Grendel slave ship had also chased a League vessel to Redoubt.
n.Highguard: Highguard grey pilgrims who had protested the Temple of the Bull in Oran were fleeing along the Lucksprings Road with Grendel skirmishers close behind. The Harvesters were also believed to be operating in Highguard-held Casinea.
n.Jotun: Jotun forces faced challenges in Sermersuaq at Pinehall Meadow, at Thoki Hawkspear's thrall camp and at Vanda Frostaxe's broken warband. In Segura, Jotun raiders from the Corazon threatened Faraden trade at the Seguridade Plain and the Kabalai Campo.
n.Navarr: Navarr vates identified a ruined way house in Vale's Lament that could become a warded stronghold. Navarr reports tracked a herald of Yaw'nagrah swelling the vallornspawn in Boar's Dell; each victory would add 500 military strength to Brocéliande's defence.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn in Feroz were hiding, fleeing to Madruga or fighting back against the Grendel. Conjunctions offered the chance to free the villagers of Ponta Delgordo and protect evacuations along the coast.
n.The League: A League fleet captain had taken a trained Mandowla from Beoraidh and vanished near Granite Isle while fleeing a Grendel slave ship. The League egregore might know more about the captain's intentions.
n.The Marches: Feni were heading for the Singing Caves mithril mine in the Mournwold and for Oakwood Monastery in Upwold. Only one of the two could be intercepted through the conjunction.
n.Urizen: A conjunction opened to Granite Isle off Optarion in Urizen's Redoubt, where a League ship had last been seen braving the rocks in a storm.
n.Varushka: Varushkan settlers needed the Druj monolith at Sullen Vale in Ossium cleansed before they could found a new vale. In Karsk, dragonbone workers offered to follow the Senator's nominee if ghouls were cleared from Mir Mozga.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's war for Sermersuaq offered chances to free captured Imperial soldiers and rescue Suaq thralls from Atalaq. The freed Suaq were expected to swear to the Wintermark egregores or become Frayed.

t.Astolat: A family of travellers went missing in Astolat, and bandits hired by The Harvesters stole the Magistrate's Grasp from a magistrate and militia.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: an Imperial orc raiding ship was blown across the entire Bay of Catazar to Feroz.
t.Brocéliande: Two conjunctions offered fights against the vallorn here. Each success would add 500 military strength to Brocéliande's defence for the season.
t.Casinea: The Harvesters, who hired the thieves of the Magistrate's Grasp, were believed to be working from the Broken Thicket in Casinea.
t.Feroz: Five conjunctions opened to Grendel-assailed Feroz. They offered chances to destroy sand crabs and their handlers, liberate islanders and save fleeing pilgrims and stranded orc sailors.
t.Karsk: Ghouls had taken over the dragonbone forest of Mir Mozga. Its workers would follow the Senator's nominee, waiving the usual 2 crown fee, if the forest was cleared.
t.Madruga: Madruga was the refuge for Freeborn fleeing Feroz across the Sorecco estuary, and the intended destination for evacuated villagers.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the great Imperial raid on Mareave and Beoraidh was the background to the stranded orc ship and the stolen Mandowla.
t.Mournwold: Feni were moving towards the Singing Caves mithril mine, where they would slaughter miners and steal mithril unless intercepted.
t.Ossium: A Druj monolith at Sullen Vale needed cleansing so settlers could found a new vale. This would be a step towards lifting the fear miasma over all of Ossium.
t.Redoubt: A conjunction opened to Granite Isle, where a League ship carrying a Mandowla had last been seen evading a Grendel pursuer in a storm.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos was the missing League ship's intended destination.
t.Segura: Jotun raiders threatened Faraden trade in Segura as a protective Autumn enchantment faded. Conjunctions offered to safeguard the garrison and a merchant's caravan.
t.Sermersuaq: Three conjunctions offered to free about 50 captured Imperial soldiers, rescue Suaq thralls and visit a broken Jotun warband in Suaq Font.
t.Spiral: A Druj warband with Vikari mages and slave artisans was leaving Screed. Intercepting it might reveal what the Vikari had been making.
t.Upwold: Feni were moving through the Silver Chase towards Oakwood Monastery, where they would slaughter the monks unless intercepted.

r.Astolat/Coombe: The trouble started in Coombe, where travellers vanished and a militia patrol lost the Magistrate's Grasp to hired bandits.
r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: In North Weaver Wood, a herald of Yaw'nagrah had empowered ettercaps and swelled the vallornspawn. Breaking its strength would add 500 military strength.
r.Brocéliande/Vale's Lament: A ruined way house at Darkening Boughs could be cleared and warded into a stronghold worth 500 military strength.
r.Casinea/Mareholm: The Broken Thicket, once used for Winter magic, was the suspected base of The Harvesters.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: A Grendel garrison held Ponta Delgordo's islanders captive. A swift strike could let Freeborn resistance evacuate them to Madruga.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Kraken's Jaw beast masters with sand crabs had landed at Valdez Cove and the Brazen Sands Forest. Stranded Imperial orc reavers needed rescue at Green Coast.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Highguard grey pilgrims fleeing from Oran along the Lucksprings Road were being hunted by Grendel skirmishers.
r.Karsk/Lestasny: Ghouls infested the Glade of Mir Mozga. Clearing them would win over Ottokar Lestasnovic's dragonbone workers.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: the successful raid on Beoraidh's port led to the stranded orc ship and the theft of a Mandowla from its fighting arena.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: The Silent Copse conjunction would let heroes stop Feni before they reached the Singing Caves mithril mine.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Settlers at Sullen Vale were blocked by a Druj monolith's fear miasma that a ritual team or priests needed to remove.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: The missing League ship had last been seen manoeuvring around the jagged rocks of Granite Isle off Optarion.
r.Segura/Anduzjasse: On the Jotun-held Kabalai Campo, a Faraden merchant and a war scout needed a distraction to reach safety. Success would slightly improve relations with the Faraden courts.
r.Segura/Anozeseri: Jotun raiders were closing on the Seguridade Plain garrison. Failure to stop them would reduce trade income from Faraden.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: Mentioned in passing: the fleeing pilgrims took the Lucksprings Road towards Segura.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: At Pinehall Meadow, heroes could challenge Jarl Heimgar to free captured Imperial soldiers. At Thoki's Camp they could free Suaq thralls from Atalaq.
r.Spiral/Screed: A Vikari-led Druj warband was leaving Screed via Tractus Animo after days on the Black Plateau.
r.Upwold/Ashbrook: The Cursed Glade conjunction would let heroes stop Feni before they slaughtered the monks of Oakwood Monastery.

Research the Terunael site of Ghita's Ve.d: The commission was issued by Harwyn Hollowwatcher, acting as Proxy of Siân Eternal, and announced by the Advisor on the Vallorn. It directed the Civil Service to carry out historical research into Ghita's Veil, a Terunael site in Segura, and comparable places such as Sobral's Stand. A report was compiled and provided to the Advisor, and the bulk of that report was afterwards made publicly available.

n.The Brass Coast: A Terunael site within Brass Coast lands became the subject of formal Civil Service historical research, and most of the resulting report was made public.

t.Segura: Ghita's Veil, a Terunael site in Segura, was the focus of the commissioned research, and the resulting report was largely made publicly available.

Smash it up.d: Inspired by a Winter 382YE judgement of the Assembly of Nine condemning eternal idolatry, the brotherhood led by the changeling firebrand Sobena Strogobor smashed the white granite statue of Janon, commissioned in Summer 380YE, to rubble with great hammers. They fled before the militia arrived and remain in hiding, though their identity is no secret. Local artist Richard Von Temeschwar dismissed fears of Janon's anger. Sobena's letter to Lady Clarice Novarion, Cardinal of Courage, offers to attack any construction the Assembly identifies as idolatrous. The civil service warns that directing such attacks could make supporting cardinals culpable, and advises consulting chief magistrate Stanislav Karkovich.

n.The League: A League-held monument, a statue of Janon arranged by the League's former civilian commissioner and paid for by Drogon Morosini, was destroyed in a criminal act by outsiders.
n.Varushka: A Varushkan warden brotherhood from Kosti has openly broken Imperial law and fled the militia, and now offers to strike at further eternal-linked constructions with the Synod's encouragement.

t.Karsk: Karsk is home to the Wardens of the Souls Road, based in Kosti, whose leader Sobena Strogobor is thought to live somewhere in the town.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar lost its statue of Janon, pulverised by the wardens before the militia could intervene, leaving some local unease about the eternal's reaction.

r.Karsk/Kopevnost: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named on the page, though it is linked as the home of the wardens' town of Kosti.
r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Hanuri's plaza statue of Janon, commissioned in 380YE and dedicated to his Vigilance, was smashed to rubble by the Wardens of the Souls Road.

The honey offering.d: A coalition led by Oksana Lyava Pinavora offered 1,000 Thrones for the Senate to relinquish the Hunt of Alderei the Fair as a Varushkan national seat. It warned that any later reversal would be a betrayal, and it would favour the Night Quarry if more money were found. A proposed Iron Roundtower near Delev would act as a mithril-buying ministry. Belakov the Wolf of Karsk vetted about 150 refugees freed from the Druj. Some 140 settled in Karsk, three proved to be monsters and about six remain unaccounted for. A commission could reopen Karsk's mines and forests for these settlers. The Iron Roads proposal was presented again. The assembly endorsed a liao mandate promoting mines and forests.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the refugees were former Druj slaves from Ossium's northern forests, and one was corrupted by cannibalism in a Druj camp.
n.The League: Temeschwar's choice to join the League, taking the Fortress of Salt, is remembered as the root of Varushkan grievance. Some Temeschwari mine owners might sell mithril at the proposed Iron Roundtower.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule freed the Druj slaves and brought them to Ivarsgard, and Karsk is recalled as having been liberated from the Thule.
n.Varushka: Varushkans were offered ways to reclaim lost Bourse seats, build a national mithril exchange, settle vetted refugees and expand the Iron Roads. Their assembly endorsed a mandate to boost the mines and forests.

t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov is not named directly. As a Varushkan territory it would share in the nation-wide mine and forest mandate and the proposed Iron Roads.
t.Karsk: Some 140 freed refugees settled in sparsely populated Karsk, many at Ivarsgard. A commission was proposed to reopen its abandoned mines and forests and create a title to mediate disputes there.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: many Varushkans in Miekarova are especially keen to see the Night Quarry returned to Varushkan hands.
t.Ossium: The freed refugees had been Druj slaves in Ossium's northern forests. Under the mandate, citizens could take mines or forests in Ossium, and mapping it with a spy network was proposed as a step towards extending the Iron Roads there.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's secession to the League with the Fortress of Salt is the old wound behind these proposals. Its mine owners might trade at the Iron Roundtower, and the Iron Roads could send more materials there and expand the Assayer's Guild.

r.Karsk/Moresvah: Mentioned in passing: Moresvah is one possible site for the offices of the proposed Karsk mediating title.
r.Temeschwar/Metri: Mentioned in passing: the Fortress in Metri once sent mithril and salt past the Iron Roundtower to the eastern vales.

The illusion of majesty.d: Estavus offered twice the usual warm ashes for ambergelt traded through Before the Throne of Estavus during the next summit. If she received more than 100 measures, she would lend bronze constructs for defence only at the Summer Solstice. The Revelry, former bandits who fought outlaws in Misericorde, sought a new patron through Erika von Holberg. Rodrigo von Mestra offered to teach the Autumn card game Threadweaver and staked his invitation to Prospero's game. The Sweetroot Bakery was put up for public auction. Laurel of Delving sought ritualists to study a bracelet found in Willstone that was possibly linked to the Lion of Arnet. The Dream-Singer offered Lashonar's Tears to the High Bard in return for new music.

n.The League: Two League-related opportunities arose. The Revelry, a Holberg company of former bandits, sought a new patron among the city's guilds and free companies, and Rodrigo von Mestra planned to teach Threadweaver at the League camp.
n.The Marches: The rundown Sweetroot Bakery in Sweetroot Town was put up for public auction because its owner, Thomas Marrowdene, needed a new investor.
n.Urizen: Laurel of Delving, a young torchbearer, found an old magical bracelet with rumoured links to the Lion of Arnet. They meant to seek out Urizen's egregore, along with autumn and day ritualists and sentinels, to study it.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: grimnir from Hahnmark were said to have kept the Sweetroot Bakery afloat by buying its sweetwater.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: grimnir from across the border in Hahnmark had been the bakery's main customers for sweetwater.
t.Holberg: The Revelry, a company of former bandits operating out of Holberg, sought a new patron among Holberg-based guilds and free companies.
t.Redoubt: A torchbearer uncovered an old bracelet of possible historical significance near their spire in Redoubt.
t.Upwold: The Sweetroot Bakery, a struggling business in Sweetroot Town, was offered for sale on the Bourse public auction.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Revelry had fought the bandit groups still infesting Misericorde's forests and recruited others back into the Empire.
r.Redoubt/Willstone: The bracelet was found in Willstone, and early rumours tied it to the Lion of Arnet.
r.Upwold/Ashbrook: Sweetroot Town's poorly regarded bakery, criticised for skimping on licorice and under-fermented sweetwater, was put up for auction in search of new investment.

The long march.d: Shadrach's mandate set the pilgrims preaching against false virtues and eternal veneration, making it harder for such beliefs to take hold, though more hidden cults were expected to come to light. Dinah's mandate, carried by Able of the Shattered Tower, sent them to convert foreign visitors, at the risk of tension with their nations. Lilith of the Chantry's mandate caused attendance to fall at every congregation outside the Imperial Orcs, possibly for years. The Navarr trod extension into Sküld raised the open question of preaching to the Thule, which awaited a further Highborn mandate. The Assembly of the Nine later endorsed the pilgrims.

n.Highguard: The Highborn National Assembly defined the pilgrimage's purpose through three upheld mandates, and was left to decide whether the grey pilgrims should preach to the Thule or leave the orcs to find their own way.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc congregations were spared the decline in attendance felt by every human nation, and few Highborn were keen to denounce them given their recent efforts for the Empire.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrians, who fled the Empire to join the Jotun after embracing the Way, were cited as an example of the faith's transforming power.
n.Navarr: The pilgrims' walking of the trods aids the Navarr quest against the vallorn, and the Navarr-negotiated trod into Sküld offered the only route beyond the Empire's borders.
n.The League: League congregations shared the loss of attendance as the pilgrims questioned human faith, and those clinging to Hatred in Tassato were named as targets of their preaching.
n.Thule: The trod extension into Sküld meant pilgrims might cross into Thule lands to convert them, which the civil service warned could harm relations; no decision had yet been made.
n.Varushka: Varushkan congregations suffered the same decline in attendance as other human nations, and the accompanying story follows a Navarr striding through Volodmartz towards Opascari.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Asavean and Jarmish merchants in every port on the Bay became targets for the pilgrims' efforts to convert foreigners to the Way.
t.Otkodov: The Navarr trod extension into Sküld in Otkodov offered the pilgrims a way into Thule lands, should the Highborn mandate preaching there.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr strider contrasts the trods of Reikos with the harsher trods of Varushka.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr strider contrasts the trods of Sarvos with the harsher trods of Varushka.
t.Tassato: Folk clinging to the false virtue of Hatred in Tassato were named among those the grey pilgrims would preach against.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr strider notes even Temeschwar is gentler going than the trods of Varushka.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: the story's striding, slowed by inexperienced companions, crosses Volodmartz towards the border.

r.Otkodov/Sküld: Sküld is reached by the new trods negotiated in the Thule peace, making it the possible gateway for pilgrims seeking to bring the Way to the Thule.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: Mentioned in passing: the story's Navarr striding is bound for Opascari, waiting for the thaw before pressing north into Sküld.

The mathematics of tears.d: The bedelaar huisbaas made slave trading a crime punishable by forfeiture and being made ongelukkig. Some slaving families fled to Asavea and Jarm, and their former slaves flooded the labour market. The Kruidenkenner herbalists offered more warehouses until the end of Spring, and an expansion of their Magazjin at Crown's Quay that would benefit four herb-buying titles. The Gjullit proposed docks at Siroc selling weirwood and white granite. Johann Van Basten offered 100 wains of white granite for 500 Thrones. The Vandersaar sought the ruined Alivetti estates in Sarvos and the Diepenbeek sought the ruins of Isember in Karsk, both by concedence. The Empire bought the granite after the Summer Solstice, and the Senate approved the Magazjin expansion at the Autumn Equinox.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel broke open Empress Giselle's tomb in the Alivetti estates during their sack of Sarvos.
n.Highguard: The Kruidenkenner already trade herbs in Highguard from their Magazjin at Crown's Quay. The High Herbalist of Sybella was among the titles to gain an extra herb purchase track once the Senate approved the expansion.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs in Skarsind are named as a northern trading partner for a proposed Sarcophan enclave at Isember.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr in Hercynia are listed among those a Sarcophan enclave at Isember would trade with.
n.The Brass Coast: The Gjullit family proposed building docks at Siroc to sell weirwood and white granite. The Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel gained an extra herb purchase track when the Kruidenkenner Magazjin was expanded.
n.The League: The Vandersaar asked the Senate to concede the ruined Alivetti guild estates in Sarvos for a Sarcophan enclave. The Master of the Clearing House in Tassato benefited from the approved Kruidenkenner expansion.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Isember was destroyed in the war with the Thule, and the Diepenbeek expected an enclave there to trade with the Thule at Krevsaty and Urdur.
n.Urizen: Under the Vandersaar proposal, the Steel Fist's ilium bounty would rise by four rings to twelve a season if the Senate conceded the Alivetti estates.
n.Varushka: The Diepenbeek proposed leasing and rebuilding the ruins of Isember as a Sarcophan enclave, building on the existing Sarcophan Mooring at Ivarsgard. Varushkan mine and forest owners might appoint a landlord for a restored Sovereign's Heart inn.
n.Wintermark: The Diepenbeek expected to trade with the Winterfolk at Kalpaheim, and the Kalpaheim Tradeholder would gain a Sarcophan purchase track once its tradehall was complete.

t.Feroz: The Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel in Feroz was offered a loose partnership with the Kruidenkenner, and gained an additional herb purchase track when the expansion was completed.
t.Hahnmark: The Kalpaheim Tradeholder would gain access to Sarcophan bargains through the northern trade network if the Isember enclave were built and the tradehall finished.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is listed as a place where Navarr would trade with a Sarcophan enclave at Isember.
t.Karsk: The Diepenbeek proposed that the Senate concede the wolf-haunted ruins of Isember so they could clear them and build a Sarcophan trading enclave. Imperial captains would be paid to secure the area and guard caravans; the offer ran until the end of the Autumn Equinox.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is not named directly; its only Brass Coast link is the Gjullit proposal for docks at Siroc.
t.Necropolis: The Kruidenkenner Magazjin at Crown's Quay was the subject of an expansion requiring 24 wains of weirwood and 48 crowns. The Senate approved it in Autumn and it was completed before the Winter Solstice.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Thule-held Urdur is named as a place a Sarcophan enclave at Isember would trade with.
t.Redoubt: The Steel Fist would receive four more rings of ilium each season, twelve in all, if the Vandersaar enclave at Sarvos were conceded.
t.Sarvos: The Vandersaar asked for the swampy, storm-ruined Alivetti estates near Caricomare to be conceded so they could build a Sarcophan dock and enclave. They offered to spare Empress Giselle's broken tomb if asked.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a place where the Imperial Orcs would trade with a Sarcophan enclave at Isember.
t.Tassato: The Master of the Clearing House in Tassato gained an additional Kruidenkenner herb purchase track after the Magazjin expansion was approved and built.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Empress Giselle's body now rests in Temeschwar, and the League there is listed as a trading partner for a Sarcophan enclave at Isember.

r.Feroz/Morajasse: The Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel's offices in Morajasse benefited from the completed Kruidenkenner Magazjin expansion with an extra herb purchase track.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Mentioned in passing: the Thule at Krevsaty are named as a potential trading partner for a Sarcophan enclave at Isember.
r.Karsk/Lestasny: The Diepenbeek planned to seek the help of the people of Lestasny so that their Isember enclave would not transgress the unwritten laws of the Varushkan wilds.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: The Kruidenkenner Magazjin at Crown's Quay was expanded after the Senate's Autumn vote, giving it and three other titles an additional herb purchase track.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Mentioned in passing: the Thule at Urdur are listed among those a Sarcophan enclave at Isember would trade with.

The price of liberty.d: Most sanctioned nations retaliated. Jarm (49 thrones 4 crowns), Asavea (46 thrones) and the Thule of Otkodov (21 thrones 2 crowns) imposed tariffs, and the Iron Confederacy closed Robec (5 thrones 3 crowns). Faraden delayed responding, but already costs 21 thrones 2 crowns, which would double if it retaliated. Incoming trade is expected to halve by Autumn 383YE. Proposals include ceding Asavean temples on the Bay of Catazar, sharing Imperial lore with Jarm and the Commonwealth, conquering Reinos, a mountain road into Otkodov, Sarcophan enclaves and a Synod statement on Justice. Naomi warns that boosting trade with slavers may undermine the Pact's purpose. Some citizens resent losing their livelihoods for foreigners' liberty.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Druj-held Sarangrave in the Mallum might lie north of Axos and so offer a possible land route, though this needs further investigation.
n.Grendel: Grendel interference hampers Axou trade across the Bay of Catazar, and Grendel control of Mareave blocks a possible Axou route via Skoura. Meanwhile Jarmish suppliers court the Grendel as eager buyers of weirwood, and a Jarmish prince sends an envoy to their Council.
n.Highguard: A ceded Asavean temple is proposed for Necropolis. Resolving the schism between Bastion and Timoj, perhaps with the palaces of the cardinals, could draw Sumaah and other pilgrims to Bastion and boost trade.
n.Jotun: The Jotun levy heavy tariffs on Faraden caravans crossing Reinos, and the Empire is invited to consider conquering enough of Reinos to bypass them. The page also notes the recent Lasambrian Jotun invasion of Segura.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast commissions are hit hard: the Towers of Anduz, already reduced by the Jotun invasion of Segura, Moonwater Hall, the Gloaming Road and the Feroz temple all suffer. A new Asavean temple is proposed for Madruga.
n.The League: Jarmish merchants in Tassato are shunning the Tassato Mana Exchange, reducing its mana. Sarvos is proposed as a site for both an Asavean temple and a Sarcophan enclave.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Marches are not named directly, though some of the affected trade commissions may touch their lands.
n.Thule: The Dragons of Otkodov, angered at being excluded from the summit, imposed retaliatory tariffs but have not yet reconsidered peace. A proposed mountain road into Erskjuvaten would restore trade but would also open an invasion route both ways.
n.Urizen: Redoubt is named among the Bay of Catazar territories where a temple could be built and ceded to Asavean priests to recover lost trade.
n.Varushka: A road north from Olodny in Miekarova into Erskjuvaten is proposed to restore Thule trade, though it would let a Thule army bypass the Grimhold's protection unless Mieriada were fortified. Karsk is suggested as a site for a Sarcophan enclave.

t.Bastion: A strong resolution of the schism between Bastion and Timoj, perhaps with the palaces of the cardinals, could make Bastion a beacon of the Way and draw trade-bearing pilgrims.
t.Bay of Catazar: Asavean granite suppliers threaten to sell to other nations on the Bay. Temples are proposed for the Imperial territories along it, and Axou trade across the Bay suffers Grendel interference.
t.Feroz: The existing Asavean temple in Feroz, held up as the model for new temples, receives fewer offerings, and the Imperial Delegate to the Temple has fewer options.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is cited as lying east of Jotun-held Reinos, which blocks the Faraden route.
t.Karsk: Karsk is proposed as the site of a Sarcophan enclave that would draw traders from the Delves and support businesses hurt by the sanctions.
t.Madruga: Madruga is proposed for an Asavean temple costing at least 30 white granite and 60 crowns, which would have to be ceded to Asavean priests.
t.Mareave: Grendel control of Mareave prevents a possible Axou trade route via Skoura.
t.Miekarova: A road from Olodny through the mountains is proposed to restore Otkodov trade. It would let a Thule army bypass the protection of the Grimhold in Perumaki.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis is proposed for a ceded Asavean temple to win back lost trade.
t.Otkodov: The Thule Dragons imposed punitive tariffs, cutting trade, raising mana crystal prices across the Northern trade network and driving up the Ambassador to Otkodov's costs.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt is proposed for a ceded Asavean temple to recover trade.
t.Reinos: Conquering enough of Reinos to let Faraden caravans avoid Jotun tariffs would negate the Faraden loss and cost the Jotun equivalent taxation.
t.Sarangrave: Sarangrave might lie north of Axos and offer a land trade route, but this is uncertain without further investigation.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos is proposed for both an Asavean temple and a Sarcophan enclave to offset lost trade.
t.Segura: After the Lasambrian Jotun invasion took seven Towers of Anduz, the new Faraden tariffs further cut the remaining towers' profits.
t.Tassato: The Jarmish enclave in Tassato is shunning the Tassato Mana Exchange in protest, reducing the mana for sale there.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is not named on the page.
t.Verthandi: A proposed mountain road would run into well-populated Erskjuvaten, needing the Dragons' permission and possibly prompting a Thule fortification there.

r.Miekarova/Mieriada: With the proposed road built, an Imperial army could attack Otkodov from Mieriada without the usual penalty, and only a fortification in Mieriada would stop Thule armies gaining the same advantage.
r.Verthandi/Erskjuvaten: Erskjuvaten would be the northern end of the proposed trade road from Olodny, and the Dragons might fortify it against an Imperial attack along that road.

The risk-all point.d: The Pact recognised hylje and daeva as persons and sanctioned Asavea, Jarm, Faraden, the Iron Confederacy and the Thule. Axos outlawed slavery with Imperial and allied aid, avoided civil war, but passed harsh laws making orcs second-class citizens. The Iron Confederacy closed Robec and its southern border and demanded that Mordecai of Zephaniah's Lament and his accomplices be handed over for killing ten templars. Faraden was angered by the sanctions, and smuggling was rumoured. Asavea and Jarm imposed counter-sanctions, while the Commonwealth and Sarcophan Delves offered trade benefits. Grendel pirates of Attar continued raiding Bay of Catazar shipping, and an opportunity to stop them was offered.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn's Lord Colwynn de Rondell and Jarrigk Orzel are named as the Imperial Ambassadors to the Iron Confederacy and Asavea respectively.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Axou fears about freed orcs are rooted in Druj invasions, and orcs leaving Axos to the north or west are arrested as presumed recruits for the Druj.
n.Grendel: Grendel pirates of Attar continued raiding Imperial shipping in the Bay of Catazar, and Grendel interference in Axos was blamed for unrest, with Issyk's new Grand Ilarch said to be critical of ties to the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Highborn fleets that traded during the season suffered production losses from Grendel piracy; the Highborn Accalon of Felix's Watch remained Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Faraden traders pay a tithe to the Jotun to cross the Lasambrian Hills, and the Lasambrian Jotun hold parts of Segura including the main route through Anduz.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast fleets were hit by Grendel piracy, the Iron Confederacy closed its land border with the southern Brass Coast, and Brass Coast businesses trading with Faraden saw merchant numbers fall as smuggling was rumoured along the western border.
n.The League: Fleets from Tassato and Sarvos suffered production losses from Grendel piracy, and Lucia Sanguineo di Tassato served as Ambassador to the Commonwealth.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are listed among the slaving nations sanctioned under the Liberty Pact.
n.Urizen: Urizeni fleets suffered production losses from Grendel piracy, and Tarquinius Ankarien of Urizen served as Ambassador to Axos as it abolished slavery.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Thanmir Hrafnar and Izsák Blár Skipstjóri of Wintermark are named as Ambassadors to the Sarcophan Delves and Jarm.

t.Bay of Catazar: The pirates of Attar continued harassing merchant vessels from territories along the Bay of Catazar, and an opportunity to end the raids was offered.
t.Feroz: The Temple of the Black Bull in Feroz continued to soften the effect of sanctions on trade with Nemoria, standing as a symbol of cooperation with Asavea.
t.Kahraman: Faraden traders were reportedly seeking routes into the Empire through Kahraman, raising concern that they were smuggling goods to avoid the new tariffs, though there was no evidence yet.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: a priest associated with the Black Sails Quay in Longbeach declined to pass on the Assembly of the Nine's invitation to Axou priests.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is named among the smaller nations close enough to affect Imperial politics.
t.Sarvos: Fleets from Sarvos that traded during the season suffered production losses from Grendel pirate raids.
t.Segura: Faraden traders who once used the Sunset Roads declined in number and were rumoured to be slipping into northern Segura to evade tariffs, while the Lasambrian Jotun held the main route through Anduz.
t.Tassato: Fleets from Tassato that traded during the season suffered production losses from Grendel pirate raids.

r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: a priest linked to the Black Sails Quay in Longbeach remarked that "we all understand each other perfectly well" and refused to carry the Nine's invitation to her sect's leaders.

The warmth of an invisible light.d: The rescuers crept over the border and freed soldiers and civilians held by the Druj. Rescued Highborn soldiers returned to their armies, but the civilians, whose spires had been destroyed or despoiled, needed a home. Three mandates were offered. A Urizeni one would commit everything to retaking Zenith, inspiring the Citadel Guard there but penalising them elsewhere. A competing Urizeni one would resettle refugees in Morrow and Redoubt. A Highborn one would shelter orphans, the sick and the wounded in Reikos. The Urizen assembly endorsed resettlement. The refugees can therefore support the Doyen of the Spires as if Zenith were recaptured, raising its cost from 15 to 20 thrones a season and speeding research.

n.Dawn: Dawn supplied a large share of the heroes who crossed into Druj-held Zenith and freed its enslaved people.
n.Druj: The Druj lost more than half of the Zenith captives they had enslaved to a series of daring Imperial raids, though they still held Zenith and were pressing into Spiral.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Spiral, which it held, is described as a place no-one would now choose to settle given the Druj attack there.
n.Highguard: Highborn heroes helped lead the rescue, and the Highborn soldiers freed returned to their armies. A proposed Highborn mandate would have sheltered Urizeni orphans and the wounded in Reikos, though no outcome for it is recorded.
n.Urizen: Many Urizeni held captive in Zenith were freed. The National Assembly chose to resettle them in Morrow and Redoubt rather than stake everything on retaking Zenith, which lets the Doyen of the Spires draw on their scholarship at once.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: bands from Varushka were among the three distant groups that joined the rescue raids into Zenith.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: bands from Wintermark were among the three distant groups that joined the rescue raids into Zenith, and the opening story follows a soldier carrying the winged lion device.

t.Morrow: Zenith refugees were urged to settle among the spires of Morrow. The territory will strain under the numbers, but sharing the burden with Redoubt should find everyone a home.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt was named as one of the two territories where the Zenith refugees would build new lives, sharing the burden with Morrow and supporting the Doyen of the Spires.
t.Reikos: A Highborn mandate proposed evacuating Urizeni orphans, the sick and the wounded to Reikos for safety, far from the fighting. The page does not record it being enacted.
t.Spiral: Spiral faced a recent Druj attack and advance, and the page notes no-one would now choose to move there.
t.Zenith: Imperial raiders crept into Druj-occupied Zenith and freed more than half its remaining enslaved inhabitants. The chosen resettlement plan means its people will rebuild elsewhere until it is reclaimed.

To loose the fateful lightning.d: Fleets based on the Bay (Tassato, Sarvos, the Brass Coast, Highguard and Urizen) again suffered a penalty when trading abroad. The Salt Lords were said to be offering bounties for Imperial ships after the raids on Dubhtraig and Mareave, and would negotiate only with Fleet Master Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra. The proposed attack would scale with the strength committed. It could end the trade penalty for a year or more, bring raids on Shayeel and Ayereed, cripple Grendel resupply, and ultimately strike Gainmeachdubh and the Tower of Tempest Jade in Raineach. Every participating fleet would be damaged for six months and earn only about half its usual production.

n.Grendel: Grendel pirates and privateers kept raiding Imperial shipping and the Salt Lords reportedly offered bounties on Imperial vessels. They faced a possible bay-wide counterattack that could sink their ships, disrupt their trade and resupply, and raid their holdings and their Spring rites to Siakha.
n.Highguard: Highborn fleets on the Bay faced a production penalty when trading abroad and could join the attack on the pirates. A Highborn captain also appears in the opening fiction.
n.The Brass Coast: With the Grendel armada focused on invading Feroz, the Freeborn corsairs were cast as the coordinators of the proposed counterattack. Their trading fleets still suffered the penalty while the pirate threat lasted.
n.The League: Fleets from Tassato and Sarvos suffered the trade penalty from Grendel raiding, and League captains could join the attack to lift it.
n.Urizen: Urizen's fleets were among those penalised when trading across the Bay and could take part in the Dominate the Bay attack.

t.Ayereed: If at least 20,000 strength was committed, Imperial fleets would raid Grendel-dominated coastal settlements here and in Shayeel, seizing mithril and ilium for the Fleet Master.
t.Bay of Catazar: The Bay was the scene of the Grendel pirate raids and of the proposed fighting, which would range across its whole length. Success could lift the trade penalty on Imperial shipping or break the Grendel's claim to mastery of it.
t.Feroz: The Grendel armada was focused on its invasion of Feroz, and the news from there was bleak, with many Freeborn fearing for kin on the eastern coast.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the recent Imperial raids on Mareave were said to have enraged the Salt Lords.
t.Raineach: At the highest level of success the campaign would end in a raid on the Grendel's grand Spring festival at the Tower of Tempest Jade, damaging but not destroying the temple.
t.Sarvos: Fleets based in Sarvos suffered the trade penalty, and pirates were said to strike at will at merchant ships between Sarvos and Veroigne.
t.Shayeel: If at least 20,000 strength was committed, Imperial fleets would raid Grendel-dominated coastal settlements here, adding to the mithril and ilium bounty.
t.Tassato: Fleets based in Tassato faced a production penalty if they traded abroad while the pirates went unchecked.
t.Veroigne: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction notes pirates attacking merchant ships between Sarvos and Veroigne.

r.Ayereed/Gainmeachdubh: If 40,000 strength was committed, Imperial privateers would raid into and near the larger Salt Lord settlements of Gainmeachdubh.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: the earlier lightning raid on Beoraidh is contrasted with this open, bay-wide campaign.

What will be, was not.d: Raziel of the Shattered Tower, Edna of the Chantry and Bartimeus all had their mandates upheld. Weirwood and mithril at auction halved, other materials fell, and white granite and ilium were withheld entirely. Faraden traders added to the distrust by claiming the auction was rigged. White granite will stay off the auction until the Senate commissions the Cinderpath Exchange, and the Constitutional Court ruled that its title could only be appointed by the Bourse. Three proposals emerged: the Invisible Cord Brokerage for Navarr weirwood in Seren, the Clever Magpie ilium hall in Kalpaheim for Wintermark, and the Hand of Guerra refugee hostelry beside the Seminary of Zemress, inspired by Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial plan to fortify the southern coast against the Grendel is cited as one of the competing demands on white granite.
n.Highguard: Following their assembly's urging, Highborn citizens withheld their white granite until the Cinderpath Exchange is commissioned, which would also feed projects such as the Virtue's Rest. The Constitutional Court ruled that the Exchange's title would be appointed by congregation owners through the Bourse, not by the Highborn Assembly.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Brilliant Shore white granite source was ceded to the Imperial Orcs along with Skarsind.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun hold the Pride of Ikka's Tears and parts of Sermersuaq, which Wintermark hopes to see freed.
n.Navarr: Navarr brokers, aggrieved that two of their three great weirwood forests are Imperial resources, proposed the Invisible Cord Brokerage. It would gather weirwood for the betterment of the nation under a Broker appointed by herb garden owners.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn assembly upheld Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra's statement with a greater majority, urging pride and support for refugees. This led to a proposal for a Hand of Guerra hostelry and a Freeborn national title to promote abolitionism.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule were ceded the Stonefield Ice Caves and the Silver Peaks, once a Wintermark source of ilium.
n.Wintermark: The mandate reminded Wintermark that it alone has no Bourse seat and has lost its key resources. The Suaq proposed the Clever Magpie trading hall in Kalpaheim to buy ilium from across the north and bring it home.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Palaces of the Cardinals would make the White City the equal in beauty of Timoj, adding to the demand for white granite.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the Heartwood of the Great Vale is cited as an Imperial weirwood resource that Navarr brokers resent not controlling.
t.Madruga: A hostelry and office, the Hand of Guerra, was proposed beside the Seminary of Zemress in Calvos to help refugees. It would need a Senate commission or wayleave, 20 wains of white granite and 40 crowns.
t.Miaren: Miaren, home of the Golden Trees, was proposed as the site of the Invisible Cord Brokerage in Seren. It would cost 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns, and would cut eight wains of weirwood from the auction each season.
t.Sermersuaq: If the Clever Magpie were built and Sermersuaq were freed of the Jotun and returned to Wintermark, the ilium available to the hall would increase, up to an option for 10 rings.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind was ceded to the Imperial Orcs along with the Brilliant Shore, leaving Wintermark without a white granite source.

r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: the Silver Peaks were ceded to the Thule along with the Stonefield Ice Caves, costing Wintermark its starmetal and ilium source.

Who benefits?.d: Phaleron offered a formal parley to Archmage of Day Skywise Gralka, open to every Urizen bonded to Menos. It also withdrew its earlier offers of an emissary and protection for the Anvil library. Lashonar opened the Caucus Forum for a meeting with the Hierro warchief. Cathan Canae demanded a parley on the Lion and Unicorn conflict, with specified Wintermark delegates and a representative of the Dawnish and Varushkan forces that invaded Ossium. Sorin rejected amity but sent a herald to question the Winter Archmage. Ephisis declined but prepared offers for the Autumn Archmage. Arhallogen's orc emissary at Lomaa refused any public meeting and said it would take 'the logical next step'.

n.Dawn: Cathan Canae required one person who could speak for the Dawnish and Varushkan forces that invaded Ossium to attend its parley armed.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: an Imperial clerk recoils at how the Druj kept prisoners in the Crawling Depths at Lomaa, and Ossium is described as a Druj territory invaded by Imperial forces.
n.Navarr: Arhallogen, the Queen of All Spiders, pointedly refused any public, formal meeting with any Navarr, and its emissary twisted its mouth at the very name.
n.Urizen: Phaleron invited every Urizen citizen bonded to the egregore Menos to its formal parley through a special portal from the Anvil regio. Urizen's Elyssiathain is named as Archmage of Night for the Lashonar meeting.
n.Varushka: Cathan Canae required a representative of the Varushkan and Dawnish forces that invaded Ossium to join its parley, which concerned the conflict between the Lion and the Unicorn.
n.Wintermark: Cathan Canae demanded three Wintermark delegates at its parley: a Suaq, a Kallavesi and a Steinr. One was to speak for the warriors, one for the senators and one for the magicians, and none could ever have championed Eleonaris or Jaheris.

t.Ossium: An orc emissary of Arhallogen appeared in the civil servants' temporary offices at Lomaa to deliver its refusal and its warning of a 'logical next step'. Cathan Canae also sought a representative of the forces that invaded Ossium.
